<a id="BIP-0038"></a>
## BIP-0038 — Encoder-heavy rather than symmetric network allocation

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** REUSED-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0024](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0024) — ByT5: Towards a Token-Free Future with Pre-trained Byte-to-Byte Models. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Retaining a symmetric subword encoder/decoder layout spends relatively much computation in a serial decoder after replacing tokens with bytes.
- **One-sentence solution:** Use an encoder-heavy 3:1 layer split while preserving the byte-to-byte training interface.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** E: asymmetric depth allocation within the Transformer; cross-attention transfers source states to the causal decoder. No parameter inversion or block tying is established.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** UTF-8 bytes plus special IDs / full-resolution byte encoder and decoder positions / byte spans or task text / span corruption (mean 20 bytes) plus supervised task targets.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** Bidirectional corrupted/full source; causal target decoder. Span corruption is pretraining, not unconditional next-byte LM. Invalid output is decoded with errors=ignore; Large-only config evidence is not runtime aliasing.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** R-FULL, §3/Table1 and §6/Table 8: sizes use12/4,18/6 or36/12; a668M36/12 variant beats a718M24/24 variant in three reported tasks. Width/size also vary, so depth ratio is not isolated. Encoder-only savings cannot establish answer-generation latency.
- **Limits:** Conditions and missing verification are included with the evidence; preserve the work-level depth and limitations.
- **Carrying scoped FULL card(s), actually read in this integration:** [old scoped FULL/BIW-0024](../../flued_multigranularity_survey_20261108/03_reading/B08/W0351.md). The source locators and numerical conditions in the retained evidence above are carried by these cards; no new FULL credited.

Replace the discovery NER latency name with XNLI; XNLI6.4–9.5× has sentence-pair input and single-digit label, XSum3.7–6.4×. Separate encoder/input work from output length. Old Large/XNLI operative gin: encoder/decoder inputs shared, decoder input/softmax untied; static configuration+Mesh definition only, no universal size/port/runtime claim.

- **Source mapping (preserved):** [S04-R002](../01_discovery/S04/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 22); [S01-R42](../01_discovery/S01/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 75); [S03-R21](../01_discovery/S03/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 51); [S06-R025](../01_discovery/S06/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 58); [S07-R12](../01_discovery/S07/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 32); [S08-R043](../01_discovery/S08/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 72).

## BIP-0044 — Selective fixed-state byte recurrence without patches

## BIP-0045 — Subword drafting with approximate byte verification

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.

- **One-sentence solution:** let a subword model draft and byte model scan/repair suggestions.

<a id="BIP-0047"></a>
## BIP-0047 — Byte chunks aligned to a pretrained subword host

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** REUSED-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0027](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0027) — When Tokenizers Fail: Byte-Level Chunking for Zero-Shot Transfer to Low-Resource Languages. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** A pretrained subword backbone may inadequately represent unseen/underrepresented language strings.
- **One-sentence solution:** Attach a byte encoder/chunker/decoder and align chunk representations with the pretrained backbone.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Local Mamba, cosine boundaries, embedding alignment, target-rate loss and periodic Hindi POS supervision; first/last backbone layers unfrozen.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** UTF-8 bytes → learned chunks → pretrained subword backbone → bytes / downstream word labels; AR + alignment + rate + intermittent Hindi POS signal. Hybrid training provenance.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** B / chunks + SW-backbone H / B, probe W-labels / LM+alignment+rate+POS; causal pretraining, probe mapping differs by interface.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** Qwen3-1.7B Urdu POS38.8→52.1, +13.3 percentage points. Hindi-trained zero-shot probe is not teacher-free/label-free adaptation; 500k sentences matched but ~1.02B bytes vs7.5M SW positions and compute differ.
- **Limits:** The evidence field retains task, unit, source-depth and budget limits.

<a id="BIP-0050"></a>
## BIP-0050 — Parameter-optimal versus compute-optimal frontier reversal

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** REUSED-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0028](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0028) — Byte Language Models: Scaling, Emergent Abstractions, and Information Allocation. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** A byte model's superior parameter efficiency may be mistaken for compute efficiency
- **One-sentence solution:** fit separate same-parameter and same-training-FLOP frontiers with complete disclosure of training recipes.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Resolution-preserving 3:1 Gated DeltaNet / Gated Softmax Attention hybrid: gated recurrent DeltaNet layers and gated softmax-attention layers supply sequence mixing without an explicit local–global–local hierarchy. Hashed 5–8-byte n-gram inputs, a wider DeltaNet convolution (4→16), and an initial four-byte mean-input/unordered-bag curriculum followed by next-byte CE co-vary. These interventions are not a tokenizer-only comparison; “dense” does not mean every layer is full softmax attention.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** Bytes plus hashed 5–8-grams / full-resolution hybrid Gated DeltaNet:Gated Softmax Attention 3:1; initial fixed four-byte mean groups / bytes or initial unordered four-byte bags / first 30% bag targets, remaining 70% next-byte targets.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** [card](../../flued_multigranularity_survey_20261108/03_reading/B14/W0356.md),§2.2/Fig.1/App.A–C. Bytes vs subwords with causal context.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** Same-parameter frontier byte better,**same-FLOP subword always better** in reported study. Byte8192/subword2048positions. FLOP counts omit hashing,loss,optimizer; no universal extrapolation to alternative architectures/training objectives.
- **Limits:** Evidence/source field retains explicit implementation and comparator boundaries.
- **Carrying scoped FULL card(s), actually read in this integration:** [old scoped FULL/BIW-0028](../../flued_multigranularity_survey_20261108/03_reading/B14/W0356.md). The source locators and numerical conditions in the retained evidence above are carried by these cards; no new FULL credited.

**Central correction (P1-02, P1-04; [correction source](../05_review/DISCOVERY_CORRECTIONS.md)):** 2610.05978v1 §1/2.1 and Appendix A.4: Qwen3.5-style resolution-preserving hybrid Gated DeltaNet:Gated Softmax Attention=3:1; flat means no explicit local–global–local hierarchy, dense is also contrasted with MoE and does not mean every layer is full softmax. DeltaNet convolution4→16, hashed5–8grams and four-byte curriculum co-vary. Appendix A.4 explicitly specifies UNTIED input/output embeddings. Fitted unique-active N includes output but excludes input/hash tables; C.2 Eq.11 operation budget counts recurrent/full attention but omits lookup/hash/bag averaging/loss/optimizer. Byte parameter frontier wins under this N, subword training-FLOP frontier wins throughout tested range; not full resident-parameter or walltime equality.

- **Source mapping (preserved):** [S06-R030](../01_discovery/S06/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 63); [S01-R45](../01_discovery/S01/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 78); [S03-R43](../01_discovery/S03/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 78); [S05-050](../01_discovery/S05/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 86); [S07-R45](../01_discovery/S07/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 75); [S08-R047](../01_discovery/S08/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 76).
- **Manual multi-label assignment:** [C12](TAXONOMY.md#C12), [C04](TAXONOMY.md#C04).

<a id="BIP-0051"></a>
## BIP-0051 — Four-byte-bag warm start before next-byte training

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** REUSED-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0028](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0028) — Byte Language Models: Scaling, Emergent Abstractions, and Information Allocation. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Learning long-range language structure directly at every byte position can be optimization-inefficient.
- **One-sentence solution:** Begin with fixed four-byte averaged inputs and unordered four-byte-bag targets, then switch to ordinary next-byte prediction.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** E: staged objective/granularity curriculum,byte n-gram hash features and wider local convolution.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** Bytes plus hashed 5–8-grams / full-resolution hybrid Gated DeltaNet:Gated Softmax Attention 3:1; initial fixed four-byte mean groups / bytes or initial unordered four-byte bags / first 30% bag targets, remaining 70% next-byte targets.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** Causal prediction under its curriculum. Flat/full-resolution means no explicit local–global hierarchy, not a pure softmax Transformer. Oracle speculation is a separate true-prefix simulation.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** R-FULL v1 §2.1/Appendix A,first30% vsremaining70%steps. Same-parameter byte frontier wins do not imply same-FLOP wins: reported compute-optimal subword frontier remains better. Target/order changes plus convolution/hash differences prevent a pure curriculum or regularization attribution. This is neither learned segmentation nor evidence of a cosine/tied output choice.
- **Limits:** Conditions and missing verification are included with the evidence; preserve the work-level depth and limitations.
- **Carrying scoped FULL card(s), actually read in this integration:** [old scoped FULL/BIW-0028](../../flued_multigranularity_survey_20261108/03_reading/B14/W0356.md). The source locators and numerical conditions in the retained evidence above are carried by these cards; no new FULL credited.

**Central correction (P1-02, P1-04; [correction source](../05_review/DISCOVERY_CORRECTIONS.md)):** 2610.05978v1 §1/2.1 and Appendix A.4: Qwen3.5-style resolution-preserving hybrid Gated DeltaNet:Gated Softmax Attention=3:1; flat means no explicit local–global–local hierarchy, dense is also contrasted with MoE and does not mean every layer is full softmax. DeltaNet convolution4→16, hashed5–8grams and four-byte curriculum co-vary. Appendix A.4 explicitly specifies UNTIED input/output embeddings. Fitted unique-active N includes output but excludes input/hash tables; C.2 Eq.11 operation budget counts recurrent/full attention but omits lookup/hash/bag averaging/loss/optimizer. Byte parameter frontier wins under this N, subword training-FLOP frontier wins throughout tested range; not full resident-parameter or walltime equality.

- **Source mapping (preserved):** [S04-R032](../01_discovery/S04/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 206); [S07-R44](../01_discovery/S07/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 74).

## BIP-0052 — Oracle accepted positions are not generation throughput

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.

- **Specific problem:** More accepted byte positions could suggest higher speculation utility even without executing a real drafter
- **One-sentence solution:** estimate acceptance under true prefixes and an unbounded proposal oracle.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Oracle simulation plus additional 200M model; not an implemented serving method. Training uses early four-byte-bag auxiliary phase then byte LM.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. - **Learning / causal permissions:** True-prefix oracle bypasses error propagation/draft overhead; no finite proposal-length throughput guarantee.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** 9.527 accepted bytes vs 9.523 equivalent bytes for token model; 3.366× is **positions**, not same-text speed. Do not promote simulated acceptance to actual speculative decoding.
- **Limits:** Evidence field includes remaining limits; no new full reading or proof certification.

Byte parameter frontier wins under this N, subword training-FLOP frontier wins throughout tested range; not full resident-parameter or walltime equality.

<a id="BIP-0053"></a>
## BIP-0053 — Attention concentration is not generated exact-copy success

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** REUSED-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0028](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0028) — Byte Language Models: Scaling, Emergent Abstractions, and Information Allocation. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** A copy-attention pattern on short ASCII phrases can be mistaken for proof of causal exact-copy capability.
- **One-sentence solution:** Keep the short attention diagnostic separate from generated full-string exact-match claims.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Source-normalized attention analysis on ten six-word ASCII phrases with five-byte words; analysis rather than a new model module.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** Bytes plus hashed 5–8-grams / full-resolution hybrid Gated DeltaNet:Gated Softmax Attention 3:1; initial fixed four-byte mean groups / bytes or initial unordered four-byte bags / first 30% bag targets, remaining 70% next-byte targets.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** B / early pooled thenbyte H / bag-of4B thenB / curriculum LM; causal prefixes.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** Source S05-050, inherited W0356 §2.4/Appendix E: no long natural multilingual generated exact-copy benchmark established; same-parameter/same-FLOP curves concern a different outcome.
- **Limits:** The evidence field retains task, unit, source-depth and budget limits.
- **Carrying scoped FULL card(s), actually read in this integration:** [old scoped FULL/BIW-0028](../../flued_multigranularity_survey_20261108/03_reading/B14/W0356.md). The source locators and numerical conditions in the retained evidence above are carried by these cards; no new FULL credited.

**Central correction (P1-02, P1-04; [correction source](../05_review/DISCOVERY_CORRECTIONS.md)):** 2610.05978v1 §1/2.1 and Appendix A.4: Qwen3.5-style resolution-preserving hybrid Gated DeltaNet:Gated Softmax Attention=3:1; flat means no explicit local–global–local hierarchy, dense is also contrasted with MoE and does not mean every layer is full softmax. DeltaNet convolution4→16, hashed5–8grams and four-byte curriculum co-vary. Appendix A.4 explicitly specifies UNTIED input/output embeddings. Fitted unique-active N includes output but excludes input/hash tables; C.2 Eq.11 operation budget counts recurrent/full attention but omits lookup/hash/bag averaging/loss/optimizer. Byte parameter frontier wins under this N, subword training-FLOP frontier wins throughout tested range; not full resident-parameter or walltime equality.

- **Source mapping (preserved):** [S05-050](../01_discovery/S05/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 86).

<a id="BIP-0054"></a>
## BIP-0054 — Boundary computational utility differs from entropy

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** REUSED-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0029](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0029) — Easy to anticipate, hard to compute: boundary dependence finds the computed outputs that entropy patching misses. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** A small patcher can assign low uncertainty to positions where a larger model still needs fresh computation.
- **One-sentence solution:** Fit a past-byte lookup table to losses under alternative boundary layouts, then combine utility-derived and entropy boundaries.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Offline layout-difference proxy or single-added-boundary scoring supplies utility labels; context table amortizes decisions into prefix-only lookup.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** Bytes → BLT-style patches → bytes; offline boundary-utility proxies fitted by past-two-byte context. Deployment causal; labels may use future training targets.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** Bytes → BLT-style patches → bytes; offline boundary-utility proxies fitted by past-two-byte context. Deployment causal; labels may use future training targets.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** BLT1B true-prefix computed-value accuracy at~10%rate:entropy19.0%, entropy+dependence67.1%; dependence alone67.8% but finalanswers4.8% versus entropy51.4%. Large-model labels are **whole-layout differences**, not single-action causal effects. End-to-end GSM8K~2% or less; offline scoring/teacher cost not fully charged.
- **Limits:** Specific unknowns and negative controls are retained in the evidence field.
- **Carrying scoped FULL card(s), actually read in this integration:** [old scoped FULL/BIW-0029](../../flued_multigranularity_survey_20261108/03_reading/B05/W0357.md). The source locators and numerical conditions in the retained evidence above are carried by these cards; no new FULL credited.

- **Manual multi-label assignment:** [C03](TAXONOMY.md#C03), [C12](TAXONOMY.md#C12), [C10](TAXONOMY.md#C10).

<a id="BIP-0055"></a>
## BIP-0055 — Encoding-level script routing before BPE

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** REUSED-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0031](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0031) — Universal Byte-Level Encoding: UTF-8/UTF-16 Routing to Reduce Cross-Script Token-Budget Disparities. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** UTF-8 gives some scripts a larger base-symbol budget per scalar even before subword merging.
- **One-sentence solution:** Route 1–2-byte scalars through UTF-8 and 3–4-byte scalars through UTF-16LE using distinguishable alphabets before BPE.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Deterministic scalar routing + BPE frequency merges; causal SW LM, no learned routing.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** Codepoint-routed UTF-8/UTF-16LE base symbols in disjoint alphabets (512) **then BPE subwords** / subword positions / subwords / next subword. No grapheme normalization.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** CP→alternate B→SW / SW H / SW / next-SW CE; fixed reversible input encoding on legal scalars, ordinary AR modeling.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** 512 base symbols, no normalization, surrogate-invalid inputs excluded; non-BMP remains four base symbols. Same vocab leaves 256 fewer merge slots than ordinary BBPE. Encoder invertibility is not validity of arbitrary generated streams; bad runs use replacement decoding.
- **Limits:** The evidence field retains task, unit, source-depth and budget limits.
- **Carrying scoped FULL card(s), actually read in this integration:** [old scoped FULL/BIW-0031](../../flued_multigranularity_survey_20261108/03_reading/B14/W0359.md). The source locators and numerical conditions in the retained evidence above are carried by these cards; no new FULL credited.

- **Source mapping (preserved):** [S05-006](../01_discovery/S05/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 22); [S01-R46](../01_discovery/S01/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 79).
- **Manual multi-label assignment:** [C01](TAXONOMY.md#C01), [C03](TAXONOMY.md#C03).

<a id="BIP-0056"></a>
## BIP-0056 — Low-label adaptation can reverse tokenizer-free rankings

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** REUSED-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0032](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0032) — A Multi-dimensional Evaluation of Tokenizer-free Multilingual Pretrained Models. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Tokenizer-free superiority under plentiful tuning data may not hold in scarce supervision.
- **One-sentence solution:** Evaluate paired multilingual models at 100/1000/10000/full-label budgets and report language/task results.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Controlled fine-tuning sample sizes; pretrained masked-LM and span-denoising baselines.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** Compares mBERT subwords, CANINE codepoints, mT5 subwords, ByT5 bytes / different model positions / NER, QA or classification outputs / fine-tuning labels after different pretraining.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** SW or CP/B / H / Y or generated label text / task labels; full-input bidirectional understanding.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** mBERT often wins low-label averages; ByT5–mT5 improves with more labels, but dense parameters differ greatly. Four controlled languages are English/Arabic/Russian/Swahili; no English-only inference to all language behavior.
- **Limits:** The evidence field retains task, unit, source-depth and budget limits.

<a id="BIP-0061"></a>
## BIP-0061 — Universal coverage is not equal positions for parallel meanings

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** REUSED-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0033](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0033) — Language Model Tokenizers Introduce Unfairness Between Languages. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Universal byte coverage is mistaken for equal context/cost on semantically parallel text.
- **One-sentence solution:** Compare representation lengths on parallel translations and dialect materials, keeping byte/code-point/subword interfaces distinct.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Corpus-aligned measurement, no new learned technique; tokenizers inherited from pretrained systems.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** UTF-8 bytes, code points, subwords counted separately / positions / no newly trained LM output / no new learning objective; parallel translations measured.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** parallel text / none / B,CP,SW counts / none; causality not a modeling intervention.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** Shan/English UTF-8 3.94 versusCP1.42; Cantonese/English .87 versus.31. Both byte and CP max/min disparities ~4.5; translations, topic and written-language lengths remain confounds. UNK-heavy models cannot win fairness by collapsing text.
- **Limits:** The evidence field retains task, unit, source-depth and budget limits.
- **Carrying scoped FULL card(s), actually read in this integration:** [old scoped FULL/BIW-0033](../../flued_multigranularity_survey_20261108/03_reading/B14/W0361.md). The source locators and numerical conditions in the retained evidence above are carried by these cards; no new FULL credited.

<a id="BIP-0065"></a>
## BIP-0065 — Prefix offsets, scalar length and frequency are confounded

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** REUSED-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0044](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0044) — Beyond Perplexity: UTF-8 Validity in Byte-aware Language Models. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Different prefix offsets and byte lengths change remaining prediction difficulty and can fake frequency effects.
- **One-sentence solution:** Stratify exact byte offset, bytes remaining and scalar exposure while using same-length unseen-character controls.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Prefix-length sweep;139 unseen three-byte Han controls versus unseen four-byte group.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. - **Learning / causal permissions:** B-prefix / H / remaining B / LM signal; prefix-only causal completion.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** Four-byte partial0/39.5/60.5% versus three-byte48.2/51.1/19.4 at prefixes1/2/3. Prefix3 completes a three-byte input but not four-byte input; script/exposure/length are not all isolated. No inference that four-byte characters are generally easier.
- **Limits:** The evidence field retains task, unit, source-depth and budget limits.

<a id="BIP-0066"></a>
## BIP-0066 — Trainable soft deletion and hard-inference encoder shortening

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** REUSED-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0046](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0046) — MrT5: Dynamic Token Merging for Efficient Byte-level Language Models. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** A pretrained byte encoder processes many redundant positions, but hard deletion cannot be trained directly.
- **One-sentence solution:** Learn a soft deletion mask after encoder layer3, then hard-delete states for later inference.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Denoising CE plus deletion regularization; proportional-integral controller targets deletion fraction; softmax1 avoids mask-translation invariance, with extra attention-score regularization.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** Bytes → surviving contextual states → bytes; ByT5 span recovery plus deletion regularization/controller. Bidirectional encoder, causal target decoder; deletion is not literal pairwise averaging.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** Bytes → surviving contextual states → bytes; ByT5 span recovery plus deletion regularization/controller. Bidirectional encoder, causal target decoder; deletion is not literal pairwise averaging.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** Soft-training/hard-inference transition matters; surviving states may already contain deleted-byte information. Not literal contiguous-span averaging, and not a causal next-byte route because source context is bidirectional and can include the question.
- **Limits:** Specific unknowns and negative controls are retained in the evidence field.
- **Carrying scoped FULL card(s), actually read in this integration:** [old scoped FULL/BIW-0046](../../flued_multigranularity_survey_20261108/03_reading/B22/W0511.md). The source locators and numerical conditions in the retained evidence above are carried by these cards; no new FULL credited.

<a id="BIP-0067"></a>
## BIP-0067 — Absolute gate signal under softmax shift invariance

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** REUSED-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0046](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0046) — MrT5: Dynamic Token Merging for Efficient Byte-level Language Models. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Adding nearly uniform gate-related offsets can be canceled by softmax shift invariance, encouraging pathological all-delete behavior or inflated attention scores.
- **One-sentence solution:** Use softmax1 plus attention-score regularization so absolute attention mass matters during gate learning.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** E: softmax1 denominator augmentation,gate-dependent masks,extra attention-score constraint (Appendix D).
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** Bytes → surviving contextual states → bytes; ByT5 span recovery plus deletion regularization/controller. Bidirectional encoder, causal target decoder; deletion is not literal pairwise averaging.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** Bytes → surviving contextual states → bytes; ByT5 span recovery plus deletion regularization/controller. Bidirectional encoder, causal target decoder; deletion is not literal pairwise averaging.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** R-FULL §3 Eqs1–7/Appendix D; these are explicit optimization components,not merely faster packing. Their role is stabilizing deletion supervision,not norm control for vocabulary logits. All encoder states being soft-masked during training differs from a hard,information-free bottleneck; no automatic posterior-collapse identification.
- **Limits:** Conditions and missing verification are included with the evidence; preserve the work-level depth and limitations.
- **Carrying scoped FULL card(s), actually read in this integration:** [old scoped FULL/BIW-0046](../../flued_multigranularity_survey_20261108/03_reading/B22/W0511.md). The source locators and numerical conditions in the retained evidence above are carried by these cards; no new FULL credited.

<a id="BIP-0068"></a>
## BIP-0068 — Learned deletion versus matched shortening and no-deletion quality

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** REUSED-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0046](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0046) — MrT5: Dynamic Token Merging for Efficient Byte-level Language Models. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Better compression than random deletion might still lose task quality or leave long outputs expensive.
- **One-sentence solution:** Evaluate deletion against no deletion, random/fixed rules and pooling at similar shortening, while measuring encoder and decoder costs separately.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Author baseline design distinguishes learned deletion from boundary pooling; operation-count model separates encoder, autoregressive decoder and cross-attention.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** Bytes → surviving contextual states → bytes; ByT5 span recovery plus deletion regularization/controller. Bidirectional encoder, causal target decoder; deletion is not literal pairwise averaging.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** Bytes → surviving contextual states → bytes; ByT5 span recovery plus deletion regularization/controller. Bidirectional encoder, causal target decoder; deletion is not literal pairwise averaging.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** Target50%:44.29→29.99ms single sequence; TyDiQA69.90/79.58→68.27/77.73EM/F1 with33.31%runtime reduction. Deletion beats matched deletion controls but not no-deletion denoising quality; long outputs amortize away source savings. ByT5 prior training not free.
- **Limits:** Specific unknowns and negative controls are retained in the evidence field.
- **Carrying scoped FULL card(s), actually read in this integration:** [old scoped FULL/BIW-0046](../../flued_multigranularity_survey_20261108/03_reading/B22/W0511.md). The source locators and numerical conditions in the retained evidence above are carried by these cards; no new FULL credited.

<a id="BIP-0074"></a>
## BIP-0074 — Small-model and intrinsic proxies for tokenizer selection

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0049](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0049) — Beyond Text Compression: Evaluating Tokenizers Across Scales. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Picking the most text-compressing tokenizer is not a reliable proxy for downstream model utility
- **One-sentence solution:** use small-model scaling consistency and complementary intrinsic metrics to predict larger-model tokenizer effects.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Six-tokenizer decoder experiments; Zipf/log-frequency descriptive features, logistic pairwise prediction, linear/RBF SVM with Platt calibration and Bradley–Terry ranking under leave-one-language-out validation. These analysis techniques are actually used; not native-byte scaling or universal rank transfer.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** Sixsubwordtokenizers, nopurebytearm / matched-backbonedecoderpositions / nextsubwordortaskgeneration / sameEnglish100BGPT2tokensubsetoneepoch, then supervisedtaskfinetuning; input/outputtied.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R08/BIW-0049](../03_reading/R08/BIW-0049.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R08/BIW-0049](../03_reading/R08/BIW-0049.md):** **Problem:** large-model tokenizer selection is expensive, and compression can fail as a proxy for task quality. **One-sentence solution:** test six existing tokenizers on matched-backbone small/large decoders and predict multilingual rankings with token-distribution features and supervised pairwise models.
- Models take English pretraining text segmented into PHI-3-MINI, GPT-2, GPT-NeoX, Falcon, tiktoken or Aya 23 subword IDs; there is **no pure-byte model arm** (fallback bytes within a subword tokenizer do not establish one). Hidden positions, outputs and autoregressive cross-entropy targets are tokenizer-specific subwords. Full decoder self-attention and vocabulary softmax perform causal next-token prediction; translation and summarization are supervised fine-tuning with source/target prompts, and evaluation uses generation or multiple-choice scoring. End-of-sequence/partial-prefix details and sampling policy are not stated. Appendix A Table 8 explicitly says **input embedding ↔ output classifier tied**; it does not imply sharing across distinct layers/models. No speculative multi-head sharing.
- **Borrowed methods and roles:** Zipf-style descriptive features (unique token cardinality; log-rank/log-frequency area; slope; deviation from linear fit) and token count evaluate tokenizer/text compatibility, not a learned model representation; features restricted to log(rank)≤6. Logistic regression evaluates held-out-tokenizer pairwise choices; a linear-kernel support-vector machine combines cardinality, power-law deviation and slope, then a separate RBF-kernel SVM with Platt calibration feeds Bradley–Terry ranking with leave-one-language-out validation (§5). This is a tiny, correlated six-tokenizer/four-language evaluation, not proof that Zipf features generalize to all tasks.

**[R08/BIW-0049](../03_reading/R08/BIW-0049.md):** All arms see one epoch of the same English-centric FineWeb **100B GPT-2-token subset**, rather than 100B tokens under each tokenizer; actual raw bytes, each tokenizer's token exposure and context in original bytes, exact context length and data filtering are not specified in the paper. Fixed 2M arm-specific tokens/batch; source data equality is stronger than equal token exposure, but total token steps and compute can differ. Nominal 350M group actually 337M–566M and nominal 2.7B group 2.6B–3.2B because vocabulary sizes vary 32k–256k, including tied table parameters (Table 1/Appendix A Table 8). For example GPT-2 356M/210 H100 h versus Aya 566M/490 h at small scale, GPT-2 2.7B/1650 h versus Aya 3.2B/2120 h at large scale. Appendix Table 7 gives 5.58 versus 8.17 and 36.62 versus 43.10 labelled TFLOPs; total vs rate/unit interpretation is not explained, so do not convert to training totals. Table 1 reports tiktoken large 2050 h while Table 7 reports 1540 h: unresolved source inconsistency. No multi-seed repeat; §Limitations acknowledges uncertainty. FLOPs, parameter and text controls are not simultaneous.

**[R08/BIW-0049](../03_reading/R08/BIW-0049.md):** **:** Table 3, visual PDF p.6, gives cross-scale Kendall τ of **0.33** multiple-choice, **−0.07** X-SUM, **0.87 (p<.05)** multilingual translation; small-model rankings are not generally reliable despite strong translation association. For translation (MetricX lower better), compression ρ=.77, cardinality −.79, AUC .77, power-law deviation .78, slope −.44; these signs reflect the metric direction, not necessarily a universal preference. For X-SUM no intrinsic feature significantly predicts performance. Tiktoken large X-SUM SL-BLEURT 39.0 versus GPT-2 43.0 (Table 4), so 'negligible English effects' has an explicit exception. For translation, Aya 350M-group average MetricX 8.7 vs GPT-2 2.7B-group 9.6 (lower better); model counts and training budgets differ. Paired comparisons: single power-law feature mean held-out F1 .70, three-feature linear SVM .76 (Table 5); leave-one-language-out Kendall τ .73–.87 (Table 6). Translation languages CS, DE, RU, ZH paired with EN; held-out is among those languages, not novel scripts or additional families. Pretraining was English-centric, whereas downstream translation uses supervised bilingual fine-tuning for 3 epochs; 'unseen' is pretraining distribution, not zero-shot no exposure.


**Remaining-field rule:** facts expressly absent in the read fixed paper/card are **unreported**, not a request to reread the paper. <a id="BIP-0075"></a>
## BIP-0075 — Realized retained text, normalization and repetition budgets

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** REUSED-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0050](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0050) — Language-Specific Effects of Tokenizer Choice in Multilingual Language Models. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** BPB changes can be confounded by normalization and tokenizer-dependent packing/truncation.
- **One-sentence solution:** Measure original-byte denominators and actual retained text, then compare per-language sentence bits on parallel material.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** 54-tokenizer/123-LM study; normalization variants and data-repetition controls; causal LM.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** U tokenizer-specific subwords/bytes and normalization → causal LM positions → symbols → next-unit loss; 54 tokenizers/123models.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** B/SW / H / B/SW / next-unit CE; originalUTF-8 B denominator even after normalization.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** Packing drops30.4–43.5% sampled text, language dependent; Chinese/German/Bengali124/159/356 B per parallel sentence. Original-byte normalization alone does not equalize semantic information or make lossy encoding a strict code for original text.
- **Limits:** The evidence field retains task, unit, source-depth and budget limits.
- **Carrying scoped FULL card(s), actually read in this integration:** [old scoped FULL/BIW-0050](../../flued_multigranularity_survey_20261108/03_reading/B22/W0516.md). The source locators and numerical conditions in the retained evidence above are carried by these cards; no new FULL credited.

## BIP-0077 — Equal-token exposure and separately reconstructed same-text controls

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** REUSED-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0051](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0051) — TokSuite: Measuring the Impact of Tokenizer Choice on Language Model Behavior. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** A same-token tokenizer comparison exposes models to markedly different amounts of language.
- **One-sentence solution:** Reconstruct an identical text stream for a smaller tokenizer subset and distinguish this control from the primary token-budget experiment.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Shared-string initialization, tokenizer sweep and text-stream reconstruction; ordinary causal LM training.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** Fourteen tokenizer-specific interfaces including ByT5 byte tokenizer / common causal Llama-3.2-1B-style states / matching tokenizer vocabulary / next-unit CE; choice scoring and exact-byte evaluation are distinct metrics.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** B/SW / H / B/SW / next-unit CE.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** Main ByT5~100GB versusGemma~471GB; four-tokenizer same-text subset requires~100–170B tokens and~95.6k–161.9k steps. Relative declines remain~.24 but **bytes are not in that subset**; no claim all14 were same-text/same-FLOPs.
- **Limits:** The evidence field retains task, unit, source-depth and budget limits.

G.2 common-text subset is Llama3.2/Gemma2/Comma/Qwen3 only, excludes bytes and does not control per-language token counts or exact batch order. C.2 PDF p.21 and HTML both say divide CE by log₂(vocabulary size): wording is confirmed wrong for BPB, not merely an HTML artifact. Fixed public commit0db0ba5648a4fa4efae010a94f69fc1042a354aa train.py→LMTransformer.forward→cross_entropy logs natural-log token-average CE; Figure 6 run/log/plot transformation remains unverified. Quarantine Figure 6 as evidence of cross-tokenizer equal BPB/equal training sufficiency. Appendix F ordinary option score is byte-length-normalized log-likelihood; exact-byte extra evaluation is ONLY Gemma2-tokenizer model,40examples/hours with Latin/SentencePiece restrictions, not14-way exact scoring. Other tasks/text-budget results are not automatically invalid.

## BIP-0079 — Cross-language and surface perturbation sensitivity

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.

- **Specific problem:** Clean benchmark accuracy misses cross-language and Unicode perturbation sensitivity.
- **One-sentence solution:** Evaluate original and perturbed questions across translated language versions and report relative declines.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Controlled approximately1B-nonembedding LM family, tokenizer sweep; human translation and model-in-loop item filtering, option-likelihood scoring.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. - **Learning / causal permissions:** B/SW / H / option score / causal pretraining, test labels; no long generated copy.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** 40 English source questions translated Chinese/Persian/Italian/Turkish plus math/STEM; non-English noise decline.21 versusEnglish.15, averaged across models. Byte ByT5 is not uniformly robust: Unicode styling decline.53. Item selection and small suite restrict generality.

<a id="BIP-0081"></a>
## BIP-0081 — Symbol-conditioned multiplicative recurrent transitions

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0052](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0052) — Generating Text with Recurrent Neural Networks. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Additive recurrent transitions insufficiently specialize how different observed symbols update a shared state.
- **One-sentence solution:** Let the current character synthesize the recurrent transition through multiplicative factors.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **E:** factored three-way multiplicative interactions condition state evolution without storing one full matrix per character.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** Restricted86character alphabet after cleaning/transliteration/UNK / multiplicative recurrent state / next restricted character / next-characterCE in transformed-characterbits, not originalUTF-8.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R02/BIW-0052](../03_reading/R02/BIW-0052.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R02/BIW-0052](../03_reading/R02/BIW-0052.md):** An additive recurrent transition may not efficiently express the conjunction of the current symbol and prior context. **Solution:** let the current character gate a factorized hidden-to-hidden transition. The full third-order tensor would be expensive; three factor matrices form shared rank-one transition components, combined with character-dependent coefficients (§3, eqs. 3–9; Fig. 3). This is a multiplicative recurrent neural network (MRNN), not LSTM gates or dynamically learned segmentation.
- : exploding/vanishing gradients and products of differently scaled parameters make standard gradient optimization difficult. **Solution:** use the Hessian-free (HF) second-order optimizer, Gauss–Newton curvature-vector products and structural damping (§§2, 3.3, 5.2). The architectural and optimization interventions are not separately controlled end-to-end against all alternatives.

Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. Only reported conditions support this record.

<a id="BIP-0083"></a>
## BIP-0083 — LSTM generation of discrete text sequences

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0053](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0053) — Generating Sequences With Recurrent Neural Networks. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Discrete text must retain dependencies beyond local n-grams while generating one symbol at a time.
- **One-sentence solution:** Train an LSTM to predict each next text element from recurrent context.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **E:** LSTM memory and autoregressive likelihood support long-range sequence generation.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** PTB49characters or10Kwords; Wikipedia205observedbyte-symbols / stackedLSTM state / same next-symbol alphabet / causal next-symbol likelihood; static vs online weight-updated evaluation separate.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R02/BIW-0053](../03_reading/R02/BIW-0053.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R02/BIW-0053](../03_reading/R02/BIW-0053.md):** Word softmax has large-vocabulary, sparsity and open-string limitations while short-memory generation can drift. **Solution:** train a stacked LSTM autoregressively on the next symbol, using memory and input-to-layer/output skip connections, then sample each symbol and feed it back (§§2–3). LSTM cell gates preserve state; skip connections shorten optimization paths; truncated backpropagation limits backward history. Word and character heads are alternate experiments, not a jointly trained shared multi-head model.
- §3.1 PTB compares **49 character classes** (4.3M weights) with **10,000 word classes** (~54M), each a one-layer 1000-cell LSTM. PTB vocabulary replaces other words with UNK; sentence-end symbol is included and scored, beginning is a null input. Therefore this character experiment is not necessarily raw original-text byte modeling. §3.2 Wikipedia instead consumes the observed **205 distinct one-byte symbols**, including multibyte-encoded characters; input/output are byte events, hidden state continuous. This is a restricted observed alphabet, not a guarantee of all 256 possible byte values. It does not describe a validator for incomplete UTF-8, EOS policy for Wikipedia generation, or a text-decoder verifier.
- Causality: next-symbol softmax given past. A sampled symbol becomes next input. Wikipedia forward hidden and cell state persist for 100 contiguous 100-byte sequences (up to 10K-byte exposure), but gradients stop every 100 bytes; reset and processing order are specified (§3.2). Recurrent weights are shared over time. Input skip matrices and output matrices are separately denoted (§2 eqs. 1–4); embedding/readout aliasing and any inter-layer parameter tying are **not specified**.


**Remaining-field rule:** facts expressly absent in the read fixed paper/card are **unreported**, not a request to reread the paper. Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. <a id="BIP-0085"></a>
## BIP-0085 — Character-CNN composition at word-time recurrent positions

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0055](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0055) — Character-Aware Neural Language Models. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Independent word input embeddings share little statistical strength between rare morphological variants.
- **One-sentence solution:** Compose each word representation from learned character convolutions instead of a word-type input lookup.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **E:** learned character embeddings, multi-width CNN, max-over-time pooling; LSTM models word sequence.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** Indexed characters inside presegmented words / CNN-max-highway word vectors and word-timeLSTM / fixed word vocabulary / next-wordCE; characteralphabet exact encoding unreported.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R02/BIW-0055](../03_reading/R02/BIW-0055.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R02/BIW-0055](../03_reading/R02/BIW-0055.md):** Independent word embeddings fail to share orthographic/morphological information, particularly for rare words. **Solution:** compose each **already segmented input word** from learned character embeddings using width-varying character CNN filters, max-over-time pooling and gated highway layers, then feed the fixed vector to a word-time LSTM to predict the next word (Model, Fig. 1). CNN detects character n-grams; pooling makes a word-sized vector; highway carry/transform gating mixes local features; LSTM carries causal word history. This is character-input/**word-output**, not byte-to-byte autoregression.
- Input unit is corpus-defined indexed characters with begin/end-of-word markers inside pretokenized words. Table 1 lists e.g. PTB 51 characters, other-language data up to 260; character encoding, Unicode normalization and exact inventory not specified. Input word boundaries and preprocessing remain external. Output and supervised target are words in a fixed vocabulary, including UNK; a composition vector can be calculated for unseen spellings but the reported experiment replaces OOV/singletons with UNK and cannot assign distinct output IDs to arbitrary new words. No byte-prefix validity or text-byte verifier exists.
- Next-word cross-entropy is causal over previous whole words, not within-word character generation. For DATA-L a two-level hierarchical word softmax uses ~√|V| random equal-size clusters; DATA-S uses full softmax. Tying axes: character embedding Q and word output P refer to different vocabularies and roles; no claim of input/output tying, shared output heads, encoder/decoder sharing, or runtime tensor alias is made. CNN and LSTM weights are reused across words/time.

Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. Only reported conditions support this record.

<a id="BIP-0086"></a>
## BIP-0086 — Source character composition and fixed-stride shortening

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0059](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0059) — Fully Character-Level Neural Machine Translation without Explicit Segmentation. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Character inputs lengthen attention and recurrent processing enough to make NMT impractical.
- **One-sentence solution:** Run convolutional filters and stride-five max pooling before the source recurrent encoder.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Multiwidth CNN extracts character n-grams; max pooling reduces positions; highway layers regulate feature flow; bidirectional GRU models longer dependencies; translation NLL jointly trains all.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** Finite300/400sourcecharacteralphabets afterMoses, RussianISO9transliteration / CNNstride5max+highway+BiGRU / targetcharacters / teacher-forcedtranslationNLL; byteencoding not established.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R03/BIW-0059](../03_reading/R03/BIW-0059.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R03/BIW-0059](../03_reading/R03/BIW-0059.md):** **:** Character sequences are much longer, multiplying encoder and cross-attention work. **Solution:** character embeddings → one-dimensional CNN with width 1–8 filters → ReLU → nonoverlapping max pool stride 5 → four highway layers → bidirectional GRU, so target attention sees roughly one state per five characters (§4.1, Fig. 1). CNN detects local n-grams, max pooling compresses, highway gates information, and GRU supplies sentence context. Pooling cells are fixed; convolutional receptive fields may overlap their neighboring cells, which is **not** learned variable-length segmentation.
- **:** Explicit subword segmentation can obscure orthographic similarities and struggle on rare forms. **Solution:** train source character composition directly against translation likelihood with character-level target generation. Table 7 provides illustrative robustness and morphology examples, not a corruption benchmark: its long German number is incorrectly translated by both systems.
- **:** Independent language-pair encoders limit cross-lingual sharing. **Solution:** pool four source languages into one character encoder and English decoder, using language-proportional minibatches and no language label (§5.5). Russian Cyrillic is transliterated to Latin via ISO-9 to promote sharing; this is an additional preprocessing intervention, not token-free untouched text. Multilingual data also adds target-English training examples, so improved translation cannot be attributed to shared alphabet alone.

**[R03/BIW-0059](../03_reading/R03/BIW-0059.md):** **Inventory handoff:** , [0087](DETAILED_INVENTORY.md#), [0088](DETAILED_INVENTORY.md#): preserve character-vs-byte distinction, filters, transliteration, target-data confounding and qualitative errors.

Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. Only reported conditions support this record.

<a id="BIP-0091"></a>
## BIP-0091 — Useful downstream representations from in-domain next-byte learning

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0063](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0063) — Learning to Generate Reviews and Discovering Sentiment. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** A low-level generative objective might fail to learn useful high-level textual representations.
- **One-sentence solution:** Train a high-capacity byte mLSTM on task-relevant unlabeled reviews and use its final state as a feature vector.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **E:** multiplicative LSTM, weight normalization, Adam; downstream L1 logistic regression decodes sentiment.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** UTF-8bytes / 4096unitmLSTM recurrent hidden/cell / next-byte, or separate sentimentclass readout / unsupervisedbyteCE and supervisedL1logistic downstreamlabels.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R02/BIW-0063](../03_reading/R02/BIW-0063.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R02/BIW-0063](../03_reading/R02/BIW-0063.md):** supervised sentence/document representations require task labels and may be limited by pretraining domain. **Solution:** train an unsupervised byte-level next-symbol model on in-domain reviews and fit a supervised linear classifier to frozen final cell states. The single-layer 4096-unit multiplicative LSTM (mLSTM) combines input-conditioned multiplicative recurrence with LSTM memory; L1 logistic regression selects downstream features (§§1–4). Input and target are UTF-8 bytes, internal unit is a continuous recurrent hidden/cell state, output is a probability over next bytes; downstream targets are review/sentence labels, not predicted text bytes.
- : recurrent optimization and context versus training memory are costly at byte resolution. **Solution:** choose mLSTM via smaller one-pass pilots, weight normalization, Adam, data parallelism and forward-state persistence with truncated gradients. Fig. 1 shows faster convergence than an equal-hidden-size ordinary LSTM under explored settings/time, not a controlled separation of every ingredient.
- : generic fixed features can plateau on larger/out-of-domain tasks. **Solution tested:** measure frozen-vector transfer and dataset-size response; no general cure established. Authors propose domain mismatch, late-document bias and linear classifier capacity as hypotheses, not isolated causal findings (§§4.3–4.4).
- : an association between a unit and a label need not control generation. **Solution:** select a sentiment-correlated cell and fix it to −1 or +1 during sampling; resulting review samples visibly shift sentiment (Table 5, §4.5). This is an intervention on one model under these prompts and choices, not a proof of universal sentiment disentanglement; negative samples can contain positive sentences.


**Remaining-field rule:** facts expressly absent in the read fixed paper/card are **unreported**, not a request to reread the paper. Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. Only reported conditions support this record.

**[R02/BIW-0063](../03_reading/R02/BIW-0063.md):** Table 1 MR/CR/SUBJ/MPQA accuracy: byte mLSTM **86.9/91.4/94.6/88.5** vs AdaSent **83.1/86.3/95.5/93.3**. CR is Amazon product reviews and authors say it almost certainly overlaps training; this is not independently verified. SST binary **91.8%** vs 30-model supervised ensemble **90.2%**, but fine-grained **52.9%** below published **53.6%**. Label-efficiency Fig. 2 averages 100 runs and uses percentile bands; labels and distribution are not matched to all baseline methods.
- IMDB Table 2: thresholding selected single unit **92.30%**, all 4096 features **92.88%**; semi-supervised virtual adversarial **94.09%**. Fig. 3 visually shows overlap between positive and negative activation histograms; Fig. 4 is six selected high-contrast examples, not an unbiased population assay. SICK Table 4: Pearson **.792** vs skip-thought **.858** and Tree-LSTM **.868**; Microsoft paraphrase Table 3: **75.0 accuracy/82.8 F1** vs metric-based **77.4/84.1**. Baselines differ in training domains, models and supervision; results do not isolate byte granularity as the cause.

**[R02/BIW-0063](../03_reading/R02/BIW-0063.md):** Table 1 MR/CR/SUBJ/MPQA accuracy: byte mLSTM **86.9/91.4/94.6/88.5** vs AdaSent **83.1/86.3/95.5/93.3**. CR is Amazon product reviews and authors say it almost certainly overlaps training; this is not independently verified. SST binary **91.8%** vs 30-model supervised ensemble **90.2%**, but fine-grained **52.9%** below published **53.6%**. Label-efficiency Fig. 2 averages 100 runs and uses percentile bands; labels and distribution are not matched to all baseline methods.
- IMDB Table 2: thresholding selected single unit **92.30%**, all 4096 features **92.88%**; semi-supervised virtual adversarial **94.09%**. Fig. 3 visually shows overlap between positive and negative activation histograms; Fig. 4 is six selected high-contrast examples, not an unbiased population assay. Pilot search and feature selection limit interpretation of a single striking cell.
- Yelp binary 598K training examples: full representation **95.22%**, bag-of-words TF-IDF **93.66%**, 500k n-gram linear classifier **95.64%**. Fig. 5 shows a plateau after ~10 labels with only ~1 point improvement across four orders of magnitude. SICK Table 4: Pearson **.792** vs skip-thought **.858** and Tree-LSTM **.868**; Microsoft paraphrase Table 3: **75.0 accuracy/82.8 F1** vs metric-based **77.4/84.1**. Baselines differ in training domains, models and supervision; results do not isolate byte granularity as the cause.

Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. Only reported conditions support this record.
