<a id="BIP-0095"></a>
## BIP-0095 — Deep fixed-context byte attention as a nonrecurrent alternative

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0064](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0064) — Character-Level Language Modeling with Deeper Self-Attention. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Character dependencies seem to require unbounded recurrent state
- **One-sentence solution:** use deep causal self-attention over a fixed byte window without cross-batch recurrence.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **E:** masked self-attention provides short paths across a512-byte context; per-layer learned position embeddings preserve position. **A:** no necessity of learned compression.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** enwik8 raw Wikipedia bytes or text8 27 cleaned ASCII characters / full-resolution 512-symbol causal attention states / 256-class next-byte softmax / next-unit CE, with training-only intermediate-layer, all-position and two-step auxiliary targets.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** Causal masking exposes only prior symbols; independent random windows carry no state across batches. Equal all-position targets, scheduled intermediate-layer losses and future-offset classifiers train representations; future targets are not future inputs. Evaluation uses final layer/final position and recomputes the full 512-symbol context without reuse.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** R09/BIW-0064, v2 pp1–4 and Tables1/3: 64-layer full-resolution model yields1.13 text8 BPC and1.06 enwik8 BPB; T12 gives1.18/1.11. T64 has235M training versus219M inference parameters, best checkpoint~2.5Msteps/175h on oneTPUv2. Prior recurrent comparisons have different parameters/compute; dynamic-eval mLSTM updates weights, unlike this Transformer.
- **Limits:** Card-attributed FULL reading is not a reproduced ablation or runtime check. Model heads are 256-way even on text8, but arbitrary Unicode legality, EOS/stopping and input/output tying are unreported. Total FLOPs, matched competitor compute and measured serving throughput are unreported; corpus-specific BPC/BPB and parameter conventions must stay explicit.
- **Carrying scoped FULL card:** [R09/BIW-0064](../03_reading/R09/BIW-0064.md); finalized source scope read as a card in this repair. All results above are attributed to that card and its fixed primary locators; no new original-paper FULL, proof certification or reproduction.
- **Source mapping (preserved):** [S08-R010](../01_discovery/S08/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 24); [S01-R21](../01_discovery/S01/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 47); [S03-R03](../01_discovery/S03/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 23).
- **Manual multi-label assignment:** [C04](TAXONOMY.md#C04), [C12](TAXONOMY.md#C12).

### Latest returned-card finding (supersedes old discovery limits)

- **Current four units:** enwik8 raw bytes or text8 cleaned27ASCII symbols / full512symbol causal attention positions / 256class next-byte head / nextunit+intermediate-layer+all-position+future-targetCE; no deployedauxheads.
- **Fixed scope:** [R09/BIW-0064](../03_reading/R09/BIW-0064.md), FULL as declared in sourcecard; actual relevant passage read here.

A deep nonrecurrent model is a counterexample to the premise that recurrent state or learned grouping is necessary for good character/byte likelihood (). The authors use causal full self-attention in a fixed 512-symbol window, 64 layers, two heads, dimension 512, FFN 2048, no cross-batch state; learned separate positional vectors are added at each layer (pp. 1–3). Input and supervision are bytes, internal positions remain one per byte, and the output is a 256-class next-byte softmax. Text8 is a restricted 27-character cleaned, lowercased English alphabet, so byte and character coincide there; enwik8 is 100M raw Wikipedia bytes with 205 observed values, not 205 Unicode characters (). Model vocabulary still contains all 256 classes. Unicode legality, EOS, arbitrary stream stopping and input/output weight tying are unreported.

- Text8 test Table 1: T64 1.13 bits/character, T12 1.18, versus 1.27 mLSTM and 1.19 mLSTM with **test-time weight-updating** dynamic evaluation; the Transformer is not dynamically evaluated. On enwik8 Table 3: T64 1.06 bits/byte, T12 1.11, mLSTM 1.24, dynamic-eval mLSTM 1.08. These are not matched-parameter or matched-compute comparisons.

Fields absent in the read paper are **unreported**; runtime/code/prefix stability not examined is **unverified**; no further FULL is required merely to fill those fields.

## BIP-0096 — Intermediate-layer deep supervision and scheduled removal

- **Learning / causal permissions:** Causal masking exposes only prior symbols; independent random windows carry no state across batches. Equal all-position targets, scheduled intermediate-layer losses and future-offset classifiers train representations; future targets are not future inputs. Evaluation uses final layer/final position and recomputes the full 512-symbol context without reuse.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** R09/BIW-0064, Intermediate Layer Losses/Training/Table4: independent layer-l classifiers stop contributing at l/(2n) of training, all removed halfway through4M plannedsteps. Text8dev baseline1.062 versus1.158 without intermediate-layer losses. Hyperparameters are reused, not separately retuned equal-budget causal isolation; training-only heads belong in training parameter counts.

Total FLOPs, matched competitor compute and measured serving throughput are unreported; corpus-specific BPC/BPB and parameter conventions must stay explicit.

<a id="BIP-0097"></a>
## BIP-0097 — All-position causal targets rather than final-position supervision

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0064](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0064) — Character-Level Language Modeling with Deeper Self-Attention. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** A stateless fixed-window predictor trained only on its final position extracts one labeled event per context.
- **One-sentence solution:** Train predictions at all positions under a causal mask, including short-context positions.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** E: dense autoregressive teacher-forced supervision over the sequence; all-position losses retain equal weight,unlike decayed intermediate layers.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** enwik8 raw Wikipedia bytes or text8 27 cleaned ASCII characters / full-resolution 512-symbol causal attention states / 256-class next-byte softmax / next-unit CE, with training-only intermediate-layer, all-position and two-step auxiliary targets.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** Causal masking exposes only prior symbols; independent random windows carry no state across batches. Equal all-position targets, scheduled intermediate-layer losses and future-offset classifiers train representations; future targets are not future inputs. Evaluation uses final layer/final position and recomputes the full 512-symbol context without reuse.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** R09/BIW-0064, Multiple Positions/Table4: final-layer next-symbol losses train all positions equally, including short-context positions. Text8dev baseline1.062 versus2.482 without multiple positions, under reused hyperparameters. Random windows do not carry cross-batch state; more scored positions are not additional unique text. Evaluation uses only final position/layer.
- **Limits:** Card-attributed FULL reading is not a reproduced ablation or runtime check. Model heads are 256-way even on text8, but arbitrary Unicode legality, EOS/stopping and input/output tying are unreported. Total FLOPs, matched competitor compute and measured serving throughput are unreported; corpus-specific BPC/BPB and parameter conventions must stay explicit.
- **Carrying scoped FULL card:** [R09/BIW-0064](../03_reading/R09/BIW-0064.md); finalized source scope read as a card in this repair. All results above are attributed to that card and its fixed primary locators; no new original-paper FULL, proof certification or reproduction.
- **Source mapping (preserved):** [S04-R023](../01_discovery/S04/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 152); [S06-R002](../01_discovery/S06/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 20); [S08-R011](../01_discovery/S08/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 25).
- **Manual multi-label assignment:** [C08](TAXONOMY.md#C08), [C12](TAXONOMY.md#C12).

## BIP-0098 — Future-offset auxiliary classifiers without a joint sampler

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0064](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0064) — Character-Level Language Modeling with Deeper Self-Attention. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** A next-byte/character objective alone can leave future predictive structure weakly supervised.
- **One-sentence solution:** Attach extra classifiers for farther future targets during training, discarding them for inference.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** E: multi-target prediction,independent target classifiers,extra-target loss weight.5; causal input masking retained.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** enwik8 raw Wikipedia bytes or text8 27 cleaned ASCII characters / full-resolution 512-symbol causal attention states / 256-class next-byte softmax / next-unit CE, with training-only intermediate-layer, all-position and two-step auxiliary targets.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** Causal masking exposes only prior symbols; independent random windows carry no state across batches. Equal all-position targets, scheduled intermediate-layer losses and future-offset classifiers train representations; future targets are not future inputs. Evaluation uses final layer/final position and recomputes the full 512-symbol context without reuse.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** R09/BIW-0064, Multiple Targets/Table4: independent two-step-ahead classifier has weight0.5 and is discarded at inference. Text8dev baseline1.062 versus1.068 without multiple targets. The supervised future offset improves the reported representation setup slightly but does not define a normalized dependent block joint or an exact parallel sampler.
- **Limits:** Card-attributed FULL reading is not a reproduced ablation or runtime check. Model heads are 256-way even on text8, but arbitrary Unicode legality, EOS/stopping and input/output tying are unreported. Total FLOPs, matched competitor compute and measured serving throughput are unreported; corpus-specific BPC/BPB and parameter conventions must stay explicit.
- **Carrying scoped FULL card:** [R09/BIW-0064](../03_reading/R09/BIW-0064.md); finalized source scope read as a card in this repair. All results above are attributed to that card and its fixed primary locators; no new original-paper FULL, proof certification or reproduction.
- **Source mapping (preserved):** [S04-R024](../01_discovery/S04/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 158); [S06-R002](../01_discovery/S06/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 20); [S08-R011](../01_discovery/S08/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 25).

<a id="BIP-0099"></a>
## BIP-0099 — Uncached full-window evaluation is not efficient serving

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0064](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0064) — Character-Level Language Modeling with Deeper Self-Attention. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** A strong nonrecurrent byte likelihood does not automatically yield practical generation
- **One-sentence solution:** use fixed-context self-attention but explicitly account for recomputing the entire context at each prediction in this implementation.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Dense causal attention directly connects past positions; multiple-target training is an auxiliary objective, **not** an implemented parallel sampler or cache.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. - **Learning / causal permissions:** Causal masking exposes only prior symbols; independent random windows carry no state across batches. Equal all-position targets, scheduled intermediate-layer losses and future-offset classifiers train representations; future targets are not future inputs. Evaluation uses final layer/final position and recomputes the full 512-symbol context without reuse.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** R09/BIW-0064, Evaluation/Results: each scored byte recomputes a new512-byte window; no computation is reused. Table2 improves text8test1.34atcontext32 to1.13at512; authors say1024did not help. This is context-window rescoring, not measured cached generation or a universal context ceiling. Best T64checkpoint175h/TPUv2 is a training cost.
- **Limits:** Card-attributed FULL reading is not a reproduced ablation or runtime check. Model heads are 256-way even on text8, but arbitrary Unicode legality, EOS/stopping and input/output tying are unreported. Total FLOPs, matched competitor compute and measured serving throughput are unreported; corpus-specific BPC/BPB and parameter conventions must stay explicit.
- **Carrying scoped FULL card:** [R09/BIW-0064](../03_reading/R09/BIW-0064.md); finalized source scope read as a card in this repair. All results above are attributed to that card and its fixed primary locators; no new original-paper FULL, proof certification or reproduction.

- **Current four units:** enwik8 raw bytes or text8 cleaned27ASCII symbols / full512symbol causal attention positions / 256class next-byte head / nextunit+intermediate-layer+all-position+future-targetCE; no deployedauxheads.

For x_i the predictor sees x_<i only under the causal mask. Training samples independent random windows; no state crosses batches. At evaluation a new 512-byte context is recomputed for every predicted byte, final layer/final position only. The authors explicitly call this expensive; no measured serving throughput is supplied ().

Training uses momentum 0.99, learning rate .003, 16 random windows/step, 4M steps, dropout .55 in attention and ReLU. Best checkpoint around 2.5M steps takes 175 hours on a single TPU v2. T64 has 235M training versus 219M inference parameters; T12 44M/41M, 8M steps, dropout .2 (pp. 3–4). Total FLOPs and comparable competitor compute are unreported.

Fields absent in the read paper are **unreported**; runtime/code/prefix stability not examined is **unverified**; no further FULL is required merely to fill those fields.

<a id="BIP-0102"></a>
## BIP-0102 — Fixed one-hot byte input and output coordinate maps

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0068](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0068) — Neural Machine Translation without Embeddings. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** A learned input/output type embedding table may be unnecessary for a256-type byte alphabet smaller than model dimension.
- **One-sentence solution:** Replace learned byte input and output embedding maps with fixed one-hot coordinate maps.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **E:** embeddingless Transformer, fixed one-hot interfaces and three learned scaling scalars; learned attention/FFN projections remain.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** UTF-8 source/target bytes / Transformer byte positions from fixed one-hot coordinates / softmax_d coordinate logits (special/unused-coordinate treatment unreported) / teacher-forced translationCE+label smoothing.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R01/BIW-0068](../03_reading/R01/BIW-0068.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R01/BIW-0068](../03_reading/R01/BIW-0068.md):** UTF-8 source bytes, including whitespace, are encoded as fixed one-hot vectors; encoder output is source-conditioned Transformer states, decoder inputs are target bytes, outputs next-target coordinate logits. Source encoder sees the whole source; decoder is causal/teacher-forced at training, conditional autoregressive translation at inference (§§2–3). No learned token embedding matrix: source and target use the same byte-to-coordinate map, positional embeddings are added, and three independently learned scalar scales cover encoder input, decoder input and decoder output. Paper says hidden width d=512 exceeds 256 byte symbols and Figure 2 defines `softmax_d(Y)`; it does not clearly explain which dimensions map to special tokens or how unused output coordinates are masked/handled, nor exact EOS/invalid UTF-8 policy. Do not silently assume a 256-way normalized byte distribution. The non-embedding Transformer projections remain learned, so this is not a parameter-free representation.

**[R01/BIW-0068](../03_reading/R01/BIW-0068.md):** Problem: learned byte embedding tables are conventional but their benefit is unclear when alphabet size < hidden width. Solution: replace the shared learned input/output lookup and unembedding with fixed one-hot coordinates and predict by direct hidden-coordinate softmax. With ordinary baseline recipe Table 2 finds higher BLEU without embeddings in 19/20 directions, tie ru→en, ~+0.5 average; e.g. en→zh 21.0 vs embedded-byte 20.2; ja→en 12.2 vs 11.4. This apparent gain is confounded: elementwise decoder-input dropout deletes the entire fixed one-hot token but only coordinates of a dense learned embedding (§6).
Problem: tokenization changes the semantics of standard dropout. Solution: test explicit decoder-side token dropout p=.2 on embedding-based controls and allow tuning it. Table 3 mean validation gains on xx→en: +0.92 BLEU learned-byte, +0.83 fixed-byte; 7/160 validation conditions decrease. Under tuned token dropout Table 4 reverses headline interpretation: en→xx learned vs fixed bytes nearly equal; xx→en fixed is on average 0.45 BLEU worse, while subword exceeds the next best by 0.76. Example ja→en learned byte 12.3 vs fixed 11.2; ru→en 22.5 vs 22.0. Thus removing learned embedding is not independently demonstrated beneficial after the optimization control. The authors' exposure-bias explanation is a hypothesis.


**Remaining-field rule:** facts expressly absent in the read fixed paper/card are **unreported**, not a request to reread the paper. Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. Only reported conditions support this record.

**[R03/BIW-0072](../03_reading/R03/BIW-0072.md):** Appendix A.1 retains a one-step-shifted input embedding residual. The shortened branch lacks current-group history but the residual supplies the previous symbol; the specific two-position-back copy construction exposes the remaining restriction. A.2 requires the extra k−1 right shift before shortening, covering queries, keys and values. <a id="BIP-0105"></a>
## BIP-0105 — Refresh unfinished prefixes without more persistent patches

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0076](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0076) — Scratchpad Patching: Decoupling Compute from Patch Size in Byte-Level Language Models. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Large patches leave coarse context stale until commitment
- **One-sentence solution:** aggregate only the observed partial patch and refresh decoder context before the boundary.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Prefix aggregation and additional trunk calls at transient scratchpad events; next-byte LM training. Persistent completed-patch sequence unchanged.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** UTF-8bytes+specials,vocab320 / local bytes,committedpatches,transientpartialpatchstates / next-byte / decoderCE+auxLMCE,auxgradientstoppedatencoder.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R05/BIW-0076](../03_reading/R05/BIW-0076.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R05/BIW-0076](../03_reading/R05/BIW-0076.md):** At prefix n, a partial scratchpad aggregates byte states from the patch start through n; it informs subsequent next-byte prediction. During parallel training every scratchpad or committed state sees itself and preceding *committed* patch states only; scratchpads do not attend one another, all have the patch's positional index, and prior scratchpads are not retained. Thus refinement is by growing the observed prefix, **not scratchpad-to-scratchpad recurrence**. Patch boundary takes precedence over an overlapping trigger. At inference scratchpad cache entries are overwritten, but local encoder/decoder computation, scratchpad working memory, and committed trunk cache still exist (§3/Fig.4).

**[R05/BIW-0076](../03_reading/R05/BIW-0076.md):** stale global context can be refreshed causally before patch completion while persistent patch count stays unchanged. Table 1, fixed p=16 NLU average 48.0→54.2 with scratchpads versus flat byte 54.1; validation FLOPs reduction 5.7×→2.9×. Increasing quality also costs compute, so persistent cache reduction is not free.
- : *where* to spend extra computation matters. Fig.7 compares models at matched training FLOPs: improvements or matches in three patchifier families, but **H-Net can regress**; appendix E.3 offers one-byte-offset router/update redundancy as a hypothesis, not an identified causal proof. Fixed-p8 entropy triggering beats fixed-stride/space-like updates on the reported quality/FLOPs frontier; dense scratchpads yield marginal code/math gains at roughly 3× training FLOPs and can be slightly worse on natural language (E.2 Fig.12).
- : a training-time trigger makes inference-time compute tunable without retraining (§5.3 Figs.9–10); language and task outcomes remain separate. FLORES-200 average rank has flat byte as strongest, SP narrows the gap (Fig.8), so English and code results do not establish multilingual superiority.


**Remaining-field rule:** facts expressly absent in the read fixed paper/card are **unreported**, not a request to reread the paper. Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. Only reported conditions support this record.

## BIP-0107 — Entropy-triggered refresh and nonuniform compute benefits

- **Specific problem:** Refreshing every byte loses patch efficiency
- **One-sentence solution:** trigger refreshes from an encoder LM entropy threshold and vary compute independently of committed patch size.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Auxiliary encoder prediction head estimates entropy online; threshold allocates extra trunk computation. Not BLT's separate offline teacher; dense updates are an ablated alternative.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R05/BIW-0076](../03_reading/R05/BIW-0076.md):** **AI techniques and supervision:** auxiliary two-layer Transformer + byte LM head estimates next-byte entropy online; threshold fires a scratchpad. Equal-weight auxiliary and decoder next-byte losses train jointly, but auxiliary gradient is stopped at encoder output (App. B.3). Entropy-patch variant reuses that auxiliary head at a separate threshold; H-Net shares auxiliary layers but uses a distinct LM output head from the router. The trunk is shared across permanent and transient states; input↔output embedding and auxiliary↔decoder readout tying are not specified. H-Net router uses MLP and ratio-loss target, not a claim that all patchifier families learn boundaries.

**[R05/BIW-0076](../03_reading/R05/BIW-0076.md):** stale global context can be refreshed causally before patch completion while persistent patch count stays unchanged. Table 1, fixed p=16 NLU average 48.0→54.2 with scratchpads versus flat byte 54.1; validation FLOPs reduction 5.7×→2.9×. Increasing quality also costs compute, so persistent cache reduction is not free.
- : *where* to spend extra computation matters. Fig.7 compares models at matched training FLOPs: improvements or matches in three patchifier families, but **H-Net can regress**; appendix E.3 offers one-byte-offset router/update redundancy as a hypothesis, not an identified causal proof. Fixed-p8 entropy triggering beats fixed-stride/space-like updates on the reported quality/FLOPs frontier; dense scratchpads yield marginal code/math gains at roughly 3× training FLOPs and can be slightly worse on natural language (E.2 Fig.12).
- : a training-time trigger makes inference-time compute tunable without retraining (§5.3 Figs.9–10); language and task outcomes remain separate. FLORES-200 average rank has flat byte as strongest, SP narrows the gap (Fig.8), so English and code results do not establish multilingual superiority.

<a id="BIP-0108"></a>
## BIP-0108 — Hierarchical predictive horizons beyond next byte

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0077](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0077) — From Bytes to Ideas: Language Modeling with Autoregressive U-Nets. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** A fixed token interface fixes both input granularity and how far each predictive step reaches.
- **One-sentence solution:** Use a rule-segmented byte U-Net whose deeper states are expanded into the following segment, inducing longer hidden predictive horizons under the same next-byte loss.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Author-used: rule-derived regex boundaries, contextual segment-end state selection, multistage causal self-attention, width-changing linear maps, position-specific multilinear expansion into the following segment and byte residual skips. Longer horizons are induced by routing/shift under ONE next-byte objective, not independent auxiliary word losses.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** Raw bytes / byte states, regex-derived word-like groups and groups of two/four such units / next bytes only / a single autoregressive next-byte objective. Multi-word anticipation is induced by shifted internal expansion, not auxiliary word-class prediction.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** Contextual states selected at rule-derived segment ends drive wider causal stages. Multilinear expansion sends a completed segment state to the following segment and adds fine-scale skips. The regex must be stable under rightward extension for online causality; actual prefix stability and runtime cache/mask behavior remain unverified. Stage padding/truncation is part of compilation, not learned boundary discovery.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** R10/BIW-0077, §§2–3/Fig2/Table2/AppendixB/C/E/H: regexword-like,2word,4word stages use selectedstates andshifted multilinear expansion under onebyteARloss. At60Btoken-equivalentdata, BPE/AUNet2/3/4 have1.8/1.3/2.5/4.2Bparams and7/5/7/8e20FLOPs;TQA26.3/20.4/22.6/15.5. H100bytes/s/GPU is TRAININGthroughput. AppendixC multlinearvsrepeatupsampling affects HellaSwag60.6→66.0; Table7wordtaskaverage36.9BPEvs33.1AU2, charaverage39.3vs42.7. No blanketequalparams/FLOPs/language superiority.
- **Limits:** No prefix-stability proof for the actual regex or code/cache certification; absent proof alone is not measured leakage. Partial-prompt/EOS flush, truncation frequencies, generation wall time, cache memory, sampling and complete compilation/tokenizer overhead are unreported. Equal average data exposure is not exact per-example context, equal parameters or equal FLOPs; non-space-delimited language limitations remain.
- **Carrying scoped FULL card:** [R10/BIW-0077](../03_reading/R10/BIW-0077.md); finalized source scope read as a card in this repair. All results above are attributed to that card and its fixed primary locators; no new original-paper FULL, proof certification or reproduction.

- **Manual multi-label assignment:** [C03](TAXONOMY.md#C03), [C06](TAXONOMY.md#C06), [C08](TAXONOMY.md#C08).

- **Fixed scope:** [R10/BIW-0077](../03_reading/R10/BIW-0077.md), FULL as declared in sourcecard; actual relevant passage read here.

A single segmentation couples representation granularity and how much future text the expensive model must anticipate. **AU-Net** uses an autoregressive Transformer U-shaped contraction/expansion hierarchy over raw bytes: select contextual states at externally specified segment ends, run wider causal attention on the shortened stream, then expand and add skip connections. Stage 2 follows regex-defined word-like units; stages 3 and 4 aggregate two and four such units, with sentence-end exceptions. The word boundary prior is **hand-specified**, not learned (§§2.1–2.2, Appendix B).

Author-used mechanisms and roles: causal self-attention implicitly composes contextual segment vectors; linear projection changes stage width; position-specific multi-linear projections expand a coarse state across positions of the **following** segment; skips preserve high-resolution signal; a byte-stage sliding window limits attention cost; fully sharded training, packing and compilation enable experiments. The multi-word anticipation is induced by shifted next-segment use, **not an auxiliary multi-token loss** (§1, Fig. 2). It is not evidence of a separately normalized word-level output model.

- Input/output and supervised events: raw bytes, autoregressive next-byte training; internal positions are bytes, regex chunks, and groups of 2 or 4 chunks; no discrete word-ID prediction head. One conditional byte chain is the reported language-model object; deeper horizons describe what those internal states must support, not extra normalized joint outputs. Teacher/tokenizer for its splits: none learned, but a manually chosen GPT-4o-inspired regex is a strong external segmentation prior.

- Table 2 p.7, 60B token-equivalent exposure: BPE 1.8B parameters, 7e20 FLOPs, 210k bytes/s/GPU; AU-Net-2 1.3B, 5e20, 225k; AU-Net-3 2.5B, 7e20, 180k; AU-Net-4 4.2B, 8e20, 155k. TriviaQA BPE 26.3, AU-Net-2 20.4, AU-Net-3 22.6, AU-Net-4 15.5. They are **equal-data, not equal-parameter or exactly equal-FLOP** arms.

- At 370B token-equivalent, BPE/AU-Net-2/3/4 use 4e21/3e21/4e21/5e21 FLOPs and score HellaSwag 70.2/69.9/72.9/73.7 and GSM8K 4.4/3.0/3.7/5.3. Across separate approximately compute-controlled scaling runs (Fig. 3), 2/3 stages track BPE on HellaSwag/ARC-Easy/NQ; TQA initially lags, and MMLU/GSM8K lag at 1e22. Neither set supports blanket superiority at matched quality and serving budget.

Fields absent in the read paper are **unreported**; runtime/code/prefix stability not examined is **unverified**; no further FULL is required merely to fill those fields.

<a id="BIP-0110"></a>
## BIP-0110 — Proposal/target correction for exact speculative sampling

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0083](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0083) — Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding, [BIW-0084](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0084) — Accelerating Large Language Model Decoding with Speculative Sampling. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Greedy matching or confidence heuristics do not preserve arbitrary target sampling
- **One-sentence solution:** use proposal/target probability correction with modified rejection sampling.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Explicit speculative execution plus exact sampling/rejection scheme; no target retraining required. Generic token model, not a demonstrated byte-serving result here.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** Genericmodeltokens / cheapdraft+causaltargetprefixstates / target-lawtokens / inheritedpretrainedcheckpoints; exactrejection/residualcorrectionnotnewtrainingobjective.; Sametokenizer draft/targetmodeltokens / distributed70Btarget+trained4Bdraft / correctedtarget-lawtokens / ARtraining plusdraftthenverify; not bytebenchmark.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R04/BIW-0083](../03_reading/R04/BIW-0083.md), [R04/BIW-0084](../03_reading/R04/BIW-0084.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R04/BIW-0083](../03_reading/R04/BIW-0083.md):** **:** Serial autoregressive target calls are slow in memory/communication-bound settings; use a cheap proposer to draft a run of tokens, score all draft prefixes with the target Transformer in one parallel pass, and probabilistically correct rejection so the target distribution is preserved (§2, Algorithm 1; Appendix A.1).
- Input/context and outputs are model tokens, not bytes; internal representations are causal Transformer states. Tested GPT-like LM uses BERT tokenization with 8k tokens; T5 encoder–decoder takes source tokens and causally generates target tokens. Supervision is inherited from existing pretrained/fine-tuned model checkpoints; no new loss, distillation or target retraining is required in timing experiments. Distillation and nonautoregressive proposers are possible future alternatives, not tested training methods here. Target and draft share a token space; their weights, embeddings, output projections, and attention heads are not asserted shared. T5-specific embedding tying is not established in this paper.
- With target distribution p and proposer q **after** any desired temperature, top-k, nucleus or argmax transformation, draft x~q; accept with min(1,p(x)/q(x)); at the first rejection draw from normalized positive residual (p−q)+ and discard later drafts. If all γ drafts are accepted, draw one additional target token. This makes 1…γ+1 tokens per target pass. Appendix A.1 proves accepted mass min(p,q) plus rejection mass (p−q)+ = p. q need not cover p: residual handles target-only support; q(x)=0 is never proposed. This is the ideal sampling law, not identical pseudorandom trajectories or guaranteed bitwise equality; finite precision and final EOS/length handling are implementation matters not specified by the proof.

**[R04/BIW-0083](../03_reading/R04/BIW-0083.md):** §4.1/Table 2: T5 v1.1 XXL 11B target, T5-small 77M, base 250M or large 800M drafts, batch 1, one TPU-v4, compared with T5X on WMT English–German and CNN/DailyMail summarization. Small draft: translation 2.6× at temperature 1 (γ=7, α=.62), 3.4× greedy; summarization 2.3× at temperature 1 (γ=5, α=.53), 3.1× greedy. Larger draft can yield *less* walltime speedup despite higher acceptance: translation greedy base .80/2.8× versus small .75/3.4×. Source/target lengths, training FLOPs and total memory footprint are not specified.
- §3: α is mean distribution overlap, not greedy string match; expected output `(1−α^(γ+1))/(1−α)` assumes i.i.d. acceptance. Walltime formula further assumes enough parallel compute, long outputs, and equal target-pass latency; extra draft and rejected-target arithmetic can increase FLOPs. Memory access to weights and KV cache can shrink, but both models and their caches must be provisioned. Appendix A.3/Table 4 shows prediction/runtime discrepancies from implementation and i.i.d. approximation. Appendix A.5's lenient mode **changes** the output distribution, unlike strict main results.
- §4.2/Table 3 reports 10k target tokens for acceptance only, including 97M GPT-like/6M draft and 137B LaMDA; it is not a 137B measured end-to-end latency result. LaMDA uses top-40 filtering. Results cannot be relabeled byte-serving benchmarks. Independently developed Chen et al. BIW-0084 uses a different distributed 70B setup and reversed p/q notation.

**[R04/BIW-0084](../03_reading/R04/BIW-0084.md):** **:** A model-parallel large autoregressive Transformer reloads weights/cache and synchronizes devices per generated token; generate a short cheap draft and score its prefixes together with the large model, then correct rejections to sample from the target law without modifying the target.
- The paper names **q target and p draft**, opposite to Leviathan et al. Algorithm 2 proposes K tokens sequentially from p, evaluates q at K+1 causal prefixes in parallel, accepts each proposed x with min(1,q(x)/p(x)), and at the first rejection samples from normalized max(0,q−p); if all accepted, draws one more q token. Theorem 1 counts accepted mass min(p,q) and rejection mass (q−p)+. No requirement that draft cover every target-supported token; the residual recovers target-only support. Apply nucleus/top-k/temperature to the distributions **before** correction. Correctness is distributional within hardware numerics, not same random seed/trajectory; algorithm's minimum target length could overshoot and EOS/stopping handling is not separately specified.
- Inputs and outputs are model tokens; latent states and KV cache are token-indexed. Draft and target use the same tokenizer and dataset; both use autoregressive training, but exact original exposure and draft optimizer/loss schedule are not reported here. Target 70B Chinchilla is pretrained, while authors train an additional 4B draft, so this work is not training-free as a whole. Input/output embedding tying, attention-head sharing and draft/target parameter sharing are not specified; no multi-byte output head. Sequence-level distillation/multiple heads are discussed alternatives, not their reported 4B experiment.

**[R04/BIW-0084](../03_reading/R04/BIW-0084.md):** Results/Table 1: target Chinchilla 70B (80 layers, width 8192, 64 heads), draft 4B (8 layers, width 6144, 48 heads; supplementary Table 2). Both served on 16 TPU v4s; draft 1.8 ms/token, target baseline 14.1 ms/token. Batch 1, K=4: XSum nucleus p=.8 ROUGE-2 .112→.114, reported 1.92× (7.52 ms/token); greedy .157→.156, 2.01× (7.00 ms/token). HumanEval 100-shot nucleus p=.95, temperature .8: 45.1%→47.0%, 2.46× (5.73 ms/token). Reported 1.92× is not exactly 14.1/7.52; retain published figures without inferring a precision explanation.
- 11,305 XSum generations up to 128 tokens and 16,400 HumanEval generations up to 512 tokens (§Results). Numbers are token generation, not bytes, and task metric agreement cannot independently establish equality of distributions. Model size, hardware and latency are given; training FLOPs, full token-data exposure and memory utilization are not.
- Figure 1: longer lookahead increases loop time, reduces fraction accepted and may increase tail latency variance; XSum nucleus minimizes mean latency at K=3, not universally K=4. A standard 7B draft served on 16 TPUs suffers communication overhead; wider shallow design is tailored to distributed residency. Attention KV reads and all-reduce costs matter; speedup is not guaranteed at large batches or compute saturation. Related Work explicitly describes independent concurrent Leviathan work; preserve both papers as distinct.

Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. <a id="BIP-0111"></a>
## BIP-0111 — Byte-prefix conditionals at arbitrary unfinished token boundaries

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0088](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0088) — Exact Byte-Level Probabilities from Tokenized Language Models for FIM-Tasks and Model Ensembles. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** A prompt may end mid-token, so conditioning on its canonical tokenization can differ from conditioning on the byte-prefix event
- **One-sentence solution:** sum probabilities of cover encodings that include that byte prefix.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Byte-Token Representation Lemma, valid-cover search and token→byte probability mapping; deterministic tokenizer construction, no retraining.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** UTF-8byteprefix/controltokens / existingcausalsubword LM andcoverstates / correctednext-byteconditional / pretrainednext-tokenmodel, nofurthertraining; canonical-support/corrected-processassumptions explicit.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R04/BIW-0088](../03_reading/R04/BIW-0088.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R04/BIW-0088](../03_reading/R04/BIW-0088.md):** **, :** A prompt may end inside the token that would encode a completed string, making canonical-token-prefix conditioning narrower than raw-byte-prefix conditioning; enumerate mutually exclusive token-prefix covers of the raw-byte prefix and use their summed probability to compute the next-byte conditional without retraining (§§2–4).
- The theoretical alphabet includes EOS as a separate symbol (not part of another token), assumed absorbing on termination; text/bytes map losslessly to unique canonical encodings. A cover is a valid token prefix whose last token covers the end of the query and whose earlier tokens stop before it. The byte-prefix event is the disjoint union of covers; `P(next byte | prefix)=P(prefix+byte)/P(prefix)` when the denominator is positive (§4.1, Lemma 1, A.2). The paper's process assumes EOS almost-sure finite termination; positive EOS probability at every step alone need not establish almost-sure termination. Special FIM tokens can be fixed as conditioning events by restricting covers to those beginning with that token prefix (Corollary 1, A.3), but this does not mean the suffix is independently observable to an ordinary left-to-right model: suffix visibility comes from the model's FIM prompt format.
- **Crucial exactness qualification:** A tokenizer-induced true distribution puts zero mass on noncanonical token encodings. Ordinary softmax models can assign positive mass to them. A.6 proposes zeroing provably invalid next-token choices and renormalizing; that improves canonical-token cross entropy under the stated support assumptions **but changes the original neural token distribution**. Thus the canonical-cover algorithm is exact for the assumed/corrected process, not automatically the raw neural model's detokenized distribution with noncanonical paths. §4.2 calls validity checks optional in the incremental step; disabling them is not a universal exactness guarantee. Invalid tokenization means a noncanonical segmentation, **not invalid UTF-8**. Lossy normalization, UNK, independent special tokens and actual vocab/decoder behavior require separate verification.
- **Mechanism/cost:** BPE/MPE cover search scans possible last-token start positions backward and tests `encode(decode(path))==path`; §4.1.1 states at most nℓ model runs for length n and longest token ℓ. Incrementally reuse existing covers and group the next byte of already-covered tokens, adding next-token candidates from the canonical prefix; theoretically one new model inference per generated byte after initialization, plus vocabulary aggregation, tokenizer and cover/cache storage (§4.2, Algorithm 3). No general constant end-to-end time/memory claim follows. A.1 relies on a genuinely fixed pretokenization boundary to cancel unknown initial-token probabilities; not all tokenizers or prefixes have one. Appendix B says an average four-byte token may require four byte decisions; §7 warns about substantial memory. No teacher, new model training or shared output head is required. Head/embedding/layer sharing in the pretrained models is not specified.
- **Units/causality:** Experiments use UTF-8 byte outputs plus control tokens; internal networks and original supervision are autoregressive subword token IDs; byte decision conditions on the raw prefix and only appropriately preceding control tokens. PSM puts suffix before a middle control marker; SPM puts suffix before the unfinished prefix, making mid-token continuation salient (§6.1). The method does not create a native byte-trained architecture.

<a id="BIP-0112"></a>
## BIP-0112 — Legal UTF-8 sequences versus incomplete stream prefixes

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NORMATIVE selected support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0090](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0090) — RFC 3629: UTF-8, a transformation format of ISO 10646. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Treating any 256-way byte output as valid text misses lead/continuation constraints and illegal scalar encodings.
- **One-sentence solution:** Validate the complete byte sequence against UTF-8 syntax before interpreting it as Unicode text.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **No AI**: deterministic encoding/grammar; useful as a validity instrument, not proof of language competence.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** Octets / deterministic UTF-8 validation state / Unicode scalars / none (normative grammar, no learned model).
- **Learning / causal permissions:** B / grammar state / CP / none; no learning; streaming prefix checking can detect incomplete sequences, complete text must end on a boundary.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** ASCII 00–7F, continuation 80–BF, legal leads C2–F4 and E0/ED/F0/F4 restrictions are specified; exclude overlong, surrogate and >10FFFF encodings. Legal output can still be wrong; grammar-derived masking would change a model's output distribution and must be reported.
- **Limits:** The evidence field retains task, unit, source-depth and budget limits.

**Evidence ceiling:** no corresponding full card was found. Retain this original source-depth claim only; no upgrade is inferred from nearby papers. Further full reading is optional unless this claim becomes a synthesis pillar.

## BIP-0113 — Teacher token probabilities converted to byte or byte-plus-EOT targets

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.

- **Specific problem:** Prefix-matching marginalization that ignores already-terminated tokens cannot preserve later-byte probabilities from a single teacher pass.
- **One-sentence solution:** Either accept approximate prefix-renormalized targets or add an explicit end-of-token symbol to preserve termination mass in the marked byte representation.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** E:Marginalize-It vsEnd-Of-Token probability conversion,teacher distribution distillation,dense byte Transformer; exactness concerns the **marked representation**,not an unmarked-byte marginal magically obtained for free.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** Subwords,UTF-8bytes,orbytes+EOT261classes / densecausalstudentpositions / sameunitor markedbyteevent / groundtruthCEorteacherKL; markedprocessnotunmarkedprefixmarginal.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R06/BIW-0103](../03_reading/R06/BIW-0103.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R06/BIW-0103](../03_reading/R06/BIW-0103.md):** All students are dense decoder-only causal Transformers. Input/internal/output are either subword-token positions, UTF-8 byte positions or byte-plus-`<eot>` positions; labels are next ground-truth units for cross-entropy or Llama-3-8B teacher distributions for KL distillation. Byte vocabulary is 256+4 specials, marked vocabulary adds EOT (261); token vocab 128,256 (§3/Table 1). Boundary markers remain part of the modeled output, not automatically the unmarked byte marginal. EOS/BOS and markers are present in the illustrated sequence (§2.2), but a complete raw-byte partial-prompt policy and marginalization at arbitrary prefix are not specified. No verifier. Inputs and outputs are distinct embedding tables **in the parameter accounting** (Appendix A Table 9 counts both), but actual tensor aliasing, shared decoding heads or checkpoint wiring were not independently checked.

**[R06/BIW-0103](../03_reading/R06/BIW-0103.md):** teacher distribution is over whole BPE tokens and byte-prefix mass may have already terminated → approximate method filters tokens sharing the observed within-token prefix and renormalizes, while marked method appends an EOT to every teacher token and includes its mass as a separate output class. Figure 2 p.5 example: after `is`, candidate `isu=.5`, `isk=.125`, `is=.125`, the approximate distribution normalizes u/k to .8/.2 and discards termination; marked distribution u/k/EOT = 2/3, 1/6, 1/6. Subsequent teacher calls are required to recover continuations of terminated alternatives when conditioning on an **unmarked** byte prefix. Exactness is conditional on the marked token history and complete token-distribution mapping, not proof of the unmarked-byte next-symbol marginal. Appendix F.1 pseudocode introduces the EOT alphabet size but does not show appending EOT to `token_to_bytes`, `gold`, or adjusting lengths; that preprocessing appears required for the pseudocode to express the prose, and is not independently verified. The released implementation was not inspected.

<a id="BIP-0114"></a>
## BIP-0114 — Observed low-compute reversal versus extrapolated high-compute gains

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0103](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0103) — Breaking the Token Ceiling: Distilling Smaller, Stronger Byte Models. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** A high-compute asymptote can be mistaken for universal byte superiority
- **One-sentence solution:** retain low-FLOP token wins and distinguish observed crossover from extrapolated ceilings.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **Used:** objective×interface scaling study and fitted downstream-error/BPB laws.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** Subwords,UTF-8bytes,orbytes+EOT261classes / densecausalstudentpositions / sameunitor markedbyteevent / groundtruthCEorteacherKL; markedprocessnotunmarkedprefixmarginal.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R06/BIW-0103](../03_reading/R06/BIW-0103.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R06/BIW-0103](../03_reading/R06/BIW-0103.md):** equal layer size and cross-tokenization validation loss do not determine downstream accuracy or equal cost → sweep 3 representations × supervised/distilled, training compute and 3 learning rates and report both observed curves and extrapolations. Models have 1.2846B Transformer-layer parameters; Table 9 totals are 1.810B token vs 1.286B byte/marked, 25 layers, width 2048. Token 2048 positions, byte 9216, marked 11264; truncate/pad to those contexts, QK normalization in byte arms, and global batches ≈0.5M **units**, not equal original text. 64 H200 per run; Llama-2 data mixture, Llama-3-8B teacher, AdamW, three learning rates 1e-3/4e-3/8e-3 and 10% warmup (Appendix A). Some large runs repeat data (§10); no total unique text, full teacher inference compute, I/O, serving latency or seed variance is supplied. The experiment ranges up to approximately 1T bytes; input counts at points and marker counts should not be interchanged.

**[R06/BIW-0103](../03_reading/R06/BIW-0103.md):** Figure 4 p.9 measured multiple-choice averages: subword leads strongly at low FLOPs; byte curves catch up within the plotted range, but ranges differ across model arms. At the ≈1.8×10²¹ FLOP 220B-token reference, all four byte models have lower validation BPB yet worse downstream than token-supervised (§§5–6). Maximum available checkpoints in Table 18 p.37: marked distilled 44.6 six-task average vs token distilled 44.4, Llama-3.2-1B 45.9 and Gemma-2B 50.3; different training exposures prevent a matched-training comparison. Asymptotic prediction at LR 4e-3 and validation set 1 is 52.4 marked vs 48.4 token distilled, a **4 percentage point extrapolation** (Table 5), not the observed 44.6–44.4 difference and not a guarantee.

**[R06/BIW-0103](../03_reading/R06/BIW-0103.md):** The two-stage extrapolation fits BPB vs FLOPs then downstream error vs BPB. Figure 21 leave-one-out sensitivity at LR 4e-3 gives marked-distilled asymptote range Δc=.0098, vs token-distilled .0025; changing residual weighting and validation set alters extrapolations (Appendix D, Figures 22–23). Validation set 2 Table 21 at LR 1e-3 predicts token distilled 49.2 vs marked 48.6, reversing the celebrated asymptotic ranking; Table 22 reports no crossover for that pair. Thus no universal 4-point gain or firm high-compute crossover is justified. Table 6's 6.33×10²² FLOPs is a *predicted* marked compute to reach token model's predicted asymptote, not a measured equal-score crossover.

**[R06/BIW-0103](../03_reading/R06/BIW-0103.md):** Marker cost is ≈30.94% more FLOPs per same source token: 4.5 content bytes versus 5.5 marked units, plus 9.44 vs 8.81 GFLOPs/unit (Table 3); the gains are confounded by extra compute and boundaries. Table 7's 6.35× text-saving and 5.19× storage-saving ratios are at that extrapolated fixed-compute comparison, not total end-to-end resources. Appendix A.6 controls saved teacher logits: token arm stores top 600 float32 logits + int32 indices, byte arm all ~260 float32 logits per byte; no free teacher computation, full online logit generation, disk I/O or 8B-teacher pretraining budget is included. §10 explicitly notes marked-byte inference can be significantly more expensive, and matched-inference-cost study is absent.

Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. <a id="BIP-0115"></a>
## BIP-0115 — Input n-gram capacity without changing byte positions

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0108](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0108) — Decoupling the Benefits of Subword Tokenization for Language Model Training via Byte-level Simulation. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Byte/subword gaps may arise mostly from the larger subword input table
- **One-sentence solution:** add hashed multi-head byte n-gram embeddings while keeping byte processing.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **E:** n-gram lookup/multi-head embedding expands input capacity; author derives from Engram demo. **A:** does not make this a retrieval-augmented language model.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** UTF-8bytes (paper512vocab,specialIDsmasksunreported) andexternalBPEhints / byteorinitial4byte-sumpositions / byte,temporarilynextsubword / byteCEwithseparatecapacity/throughput/boundary/position/normalization/targetinterventions.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R08/BIW-0108](../03_reading/R08/BIW-0108.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R08/BIW-0108](../03_reading/R08/BIW-0108.md):** ** / capacity:** use Engram-inspired multihead input n-gram lookup as a capacity intervention, not a change in output alphabet: max n=3, eight heads, base 15k buckets/order, 71,065,088 added parameters (§5.1, Table 2). Figure 1 shows a small byte-loss improvement at 1.7B, Figure 7a a larger gap at 68M. No full embedding-capacity factorial or tied-vs-untied ablation.
- ** / throughput:** sum each consecutive four byte embeddings into one latent position, predict only the first byte of the *next* group for 50k steps then return to ordinary byte training (§5.2, Fig. 2). The first 50k stage suppresses 3/4 targets and changes sequence order/representation and raw context as well as exposure. Following switch validation loss drops below baseline: visually ~0.78 vs ~0.80 immediately before late decay near 90k, and ~0.74 vs ~0.76 at 100k. These are approximate from curves, not proof of independent throughput causation.
- **/0118 / boundaries:** binary embeddings for BPE starts or ends are added to byte input; §5.3 claims start boundaries are causal and ends leak future information. An offline tokenizer can revise earlier starts when a future byte changes previous segmentation; the paper does not establish prefix consistency of starts, hence do not endorse a general causality claim. Fig. 3a end labels have bigger advantage while supplied at evaluation, but are privileged; Fig. 3b training-only 50k then withdrawal shows start-arm post-switch below baseline and end-arm near baseline. Validation during initial intervention is without the hints for the training-only curves; the discontinuities should not be read as identical evaluation regimes. Labels come from an external tokenizer, not a learned verifier.
- ** / position:** repeat subword index over constituent bytes as RoPE position (§5.4). Fig. 4a shows a modest gain with hints; Fig. 4b after reverting at 50k is worse than baseline for much of the remaining run, so no durable advantage established. Since offline IDs derive from segmentation starts, prefix consistency is likewise unverified. Repeated indices encode an external boundary prior rather than byte distances.
- ** / normalization:** keep byte chain but normalize accumulated next-byte log-loss by subword count instead of byte count (§5.5). Figure 5 near-overlap: small improvement, not evidence that changing output-unit family has no effect. Paper's algebra is for decomposing probability under the byte model and same context, not a proof that a separately trained subword softmax has that probability or that normalization turns canonical token path probability into marginal text probability. Variable M/N across batches can alter weighting, not just a global learning-rate factor.
- ** / subword prediction:** temporary separate next-subword softmax targets at end-of-subword states for 50k then revert to byte output (§5.6); Figure 6 remains worse near 100k (~.79 vs ~.76), with transition/unused-head confounds. It is not a negative result on all multi-byte prediction or a proven exact byte likelihood. BPE-derived target boundaries and training-time head create a different supervision budget.


**Remaining-field rule:** facts expressly absent in the read fixed paper/card are **unreported**, not a request to reread the paper. <a id="BIP-0116"></a>
## BIP-0116 — Temporary four-byte throughput curriculum changes supervision

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0108](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0108) — Decoupling the Benefits of Subword Tokenization for Language Model Training via Byte-level Simulation. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Equal symbol counts expose byte models to much less text than subword models
- **One-sentence solution:** temporarily pool four bytes per position and predict the first byte of the next chunk to raise raw-text throughput.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **E:** fixed sum pooling and training curriculum; changes both exposure and prediction task. **A:** not a perfectly isolated sample-throughput-only causal manipulation.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** UTF-8bytes (paper512vocab,specialIDsmasksunreported) andexternalBPEhints / byteorinitial4byte-sumpositions / byte,temporarilynextsubword / byteCEwithseparatecapacity/throughput/boundary/position/normalization/targetinterventions.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R08/BIW-0108](../03_reading/R08/BIW-0108.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R08/BIW-0108](../03_reading/R08/BIW-0108.md):** ** / capacity:** use Engram-inspired multihead input n-gram lookup as a capacity intervention, not a change in output alphabet: max n=3, eight heads, base 15k buckets/order, 71,065,088 added parameters (§5.1, Table 2). Figure 1 shows a small byte-loss improvement at 1.7B, Figure 7a a larger gap at 68M. No full embedding-capacity factorial or tied-vs-untied ablation.
- ** / throughput:** sum each consecutive four byte embeddings into one latent position, predict only the first byte of the *next* group for 50k steps then return to ordinary byte training (§5.2, Fig. 2). The first 50k stage suppresses 3/4 targets and changes sequence order/representation and raw context as well as exposure. Following switch validation loss drops below baseline: visually ~0.78 vs ~0.80 immediately before late decay near 90k, and ~0.74 vs ~0.76 at 100k. These are approximate from curves, not proof of independent throughput causation.
- **/0118 / boundaries:** binary embeddings for BPE starts or ends are added to byte input; §5.3 claims start boundaries are causal and ends leak future information. An offline tokenizer can revise earlier starts when a future byte changes previous segmentation; the paper does not establish prefix consistency of starts, hence do not endorse a general causality claim. Fig. 3a end labels have bigger advantage while supplied at evaluation, but are privileged; Fig. 3b training-only 50k then withdrawal shows start-arm post-switch below baseline and end-arm near baseline. Validation during initial intervention is without the hints for the training-only curves; the discontinuities should not be read as identical evaluation regimes. Labels come from an external tokenizer, not a learned verifier.
- ** / position:** repeat subword index over constituent bytes as RoPE position (§5.4). Fig. 4a shows a modest gain with hints; Fig. 4b after reverting at 50k is worse than baseline for much of the remaining run, so no durable advantage established. Since offline IDs derive from segmentation starts, prefix consistency is likewise unverified. Repeated indices encode an external boundary prior rather than byte distances.
- ** / normalization:** keep byte chain but normalize accumulated next-byte log-loss by subword count instead of byte count (§5.5). Figure 5 near-overlap: small improvement, not evidence that changing output-unit family has no effect. Paper's algebra is for decomposing probability under the byte model and same context, not a proof that a separately trained subword softmax has that probability or that normalization turns canonical token path probability into marginal text probability. Variable M/N across batches can alter weighting, not just a global learning-rate factor.
- ** / subword prediction:** temporary separate next-subword softmax targets at end-of-subword states for 50k then revert to byte output (§5.6); Figure 6 remains worse near 100k (~.79 vs ~.76), with transition/unused-head confounds. It is not a negative result on all multi-byte prediction or a proven exact byte likelihood. BPE-derived target boundaries and training-time head create a different supervision budget.

Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. Only reported conditions support this record.
