<a id="BIP-0120"></a>
## BIP-0120 — Temporary next-subword head as a negative supervision result

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0108](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0108) — Decoupling the Benefits of Subword Tokenization for Language Model Training via Byte-level Simulation. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** A subword target may help because it predicts a variable-length future chunk at once
- **One-sentence solution:** temporarily train a byte-input model with a next-subword output head at end boundaries, then return to byte prediction.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **E:** alternate prediction head/target curriculum; author compares to multi-token prediction. **A:** that comparison is an author analogy, not equivalence to a joint byte model.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** UTF-8bytes (paper512vocab,specialIDsmasksunreported) andexternalBPEhints / byteorinitial4byte-sumpositions / byte,temporarilynextsubword / byteCEwithseparatecapacity/throughput/boundary/position/normalization/targetinterventions.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R08/BIW-0108](../03_reading/R08/BIW-0108.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R08/BIW-0108](../03_reading/R08/BIW-0108.md):** ** / capacity:** use Engram-inspired multihead input n-gram lookup as a capacity intervention, not a change in output alphabet: max n=3, eight heads, base 15k buckets/order, 71,065,088 added parameters (§5.1, Table 2). Figure 1 shows a small byte-loss improvement at 1.7B, Figure 7a a larger gap at 68M. No full embedding-capacity factorial or tied-vs-untied ablation.
- ** / throughput:** sum each consecutive four byte embeddings into one latent position, predict only the first byte of the *next* group for 50k steps then return to ordinary byte training (§5.2, Fig. 2). The first 50k stage suppresses 3/4 targets and changes sequence order/representation and raw context as well as exposure. Following switch validation loss drops below baseline: visually ~0.78 vs ~0.80 immediately before late decay near 90k, and ~0.74 vs ~0.76 at 100k. These are approximate from curves, not proof of independent throughput causation.
- **/0118 / boundaries:** binary embeddings for BPE starts or ends are added to byte input; §5.3 claims start boundaries are causal and ends leak future information. An offline tokenizer can revise earlier starts when a future byte changes previous segmentation; the paper does not establish prefix consistency of starts, hence do not endorse a general causality claim. Fig. 3a end labels have bigger advantage while supplied at evaluation, but are privileged; Fig. 3b training-only 50k then withdrawal shows start-arm post-switch below baseline and end-arm near baseline. Validation during initial intervention is without the hints for the training-only curves; the discontinuities should not be read as identical evaluation regimes. Labels come from an external tokenizer, not a learned verifier.
- ** / position:** repeat subword index over constituent bytes as RoPE position (§5.4). Fig. 4a shows a modest gain with hints; Fig. 4b after reverting at 50k is worse than baseline for much of the remaining run, so no durable advantage established. Since offline IDs derive from segmentation starts, prefix consistency is likewise unverified. Repeated indices encode an external boundary prior rather than byte distances.
- ** / normalization:** keep byte chain but normalize accumulated next-byte log-loss by subword count instead of byte count (§5.5). Figure 5 near-overlap: small improvement, not evidence that changing output-unit family has no effect. Paper's algebra is for decomposing probability under the byte model and same context, not a proof that a separately trained subword softmax has that probability or that normalization turns canonical token path probability into marginal text probability. Variable M/N across batches can alter weighting, not just a global learning-rate factor.
- ** / subword prediction:** temporary separate next-subword softmax targets at end-of-subword states for 50k then revert to byte output (§5.6); Figure 6 remains worse near 100k (~.79 vs ~.76), with transition/unused-head confounds. It is not a negative result on all multi-byte prediction or a proven exact byte likelihood. BPE-derived target boundaries and training-time head create a different supervision budget.

<a id="BIP-0121"></a>
## BIP-0121 — Cross-attention into a fixed latent compute array

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0117](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0117) — Perceiver IO: A General Architecture for Structured Inputs & Outputs. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Raw-byte input length makes repeatedly applying full-resolution attention costly
- **One-sentence solution:** cross-attend into a fixed latent array, process it deeply, then query outputs from latents.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Encoder cross-attention performs learned input aggregation; latent self-attention decouples deep compute from input length; output cross-attention produces byte-position or task outputs. No requirement of contiguous token-like groups.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** 2048UTF-8bytes or512SentencePiece / 256learned latent slots, deep latent selfattention / masked byte/subword IDs or query-specific task labels / 15%whitespace-word corruption,MLM and task labels.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R01/BIW-0117](../03_reading/R01/BIW-0117.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R01/BIW-0117](../03_reading/R01/BIW-0117.md):** Long bytes cause quadratic full-sequence attention: map inputs to a fixed-size latent attention workspace before deep processing. Table 1: FLOP-matched byte BERT 6 layers, 20M, 130B FLOPs, 2.9 training steps/s, GLUE 71.5; byte Perceiver 26 layers, 201M, 113B, 7.6 steps/s, 81.0. This is ~2.62× training step rate under the reported setup, not an equal-parameter comparison or generative serving benchmark. The FLOPs are theoretical inference-style model operations; Appendix D counts multiplies and adds separately. Exact language hardware is not stated in the language appendix; do not assume ImageNet's 64 TPUv3. Both use batch 2048 and the same optimization schedule, but raw text identity between tokenizations is not established.
Outputs of different shapes need not inherit input indexing: query the latent with output positions or task vectors. SentencePiece BERT 110M/109B/81.1 vs byte Perceiver 201M/113B/81.0; same approximate compute, not same total parameters. Multitask query 81.8 vs separate-task 81.0 (Table 2), but train protocols differ. Standard task output heads remain task-specific; query/readout flexibility is not evidence of a shared generative vocabulary projection.
Byte-level language representations may suffer information loss through the latent bottleneck. Appendix F Table 15: at roughly matched FLOPs, N=128,width 1920 gives 75.84 GLUE versus N=256,width 1280 gives 80.95 and N=512,width 896 gives 80.92; neither N nor width varies independently. A compact workspace is not automatically adequate. Table 14 shows task-level differences; e.g. byte IO++ MNLI matched 84.13 vs token BERT 85.56, even though overall IO++ 81.76 vs 81.14. English-only GLUE is not multilingual evidence.
Query-based access exposes output-specific selection without rereading original source after encoding, but all source information available to outputs must already be in latents. Appendix F Figure 7 shows content- and position-selective encoder attention; it is not evidence of lossless storage or a multi-hop causal retrieval guarantee. Non-language Appendix I reports that even parallel output batching cannot avoid simultaneously encoding all inputs.

Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. <a id="BIP-0122"></a>
## BIP-0122 — Whole-word corruption with byte prediction targets

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0117](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0117) — Perceiver IO: A General Architecture for Structured Inputs & Outputs. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Isolated-byte masking may permit trivial local reconstruction
- **One-sentence solution:** mask whole space-delimited words even when input/output symbols are bytes.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **Used:** word-based corruption selection, byte-wise softmax CE at masked positions.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** 2048UTF-8bytes or512SentencePiece / 256learned latent slots, deep latent selfattention / masked byte/subword IDs or query-specific task labels / 15%whitespace-word corruption,MLM and task labels.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R01/BIW-0117](../03_reading/R01/BIW-0117.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R01/BIW-0117](../03_reading/R01/BIW-0117.md):** Language input is 2048 UTF-8 bytes plus special tokens or 512 SentencePiece tokens, with learned position features; 256 bytes + 4 specials. Internal representation is 256 latent vectors width 1280 for 26 processing layers (IO++) uses 40 layers and width 1536). Pretraining output queries are learned position-specific vectors; paper's Table 11 gives O=2048 or 512 queries although §4.1 describes one per masked input. Loss predicts masked byte or token identity, a classification output, and 15% whitespace-delimited words are selected for masking (§4.1, Appendix F.2–F.3). Input is the full corrupted sequence. The query position need not expose the gold byte, but the latent can contain right-hand **unmasked** context; this is bidirectional masked prediction, not a left-to-right byte probability or generative decoder. Downstream GLUE outputs use task-specific queries and classification/regression heads. EOS, partial byte prefix, sampling, verifier and inference-cache policy are not reported.

**[R01/BIW-0117](../03_reading/R01/BIW-0117.md):** **Pretraining:** C4/English Wikipedia 70/30 token mixture, concatenate 10 documents then crop, 500k steps × 2048 batch, LAMB LR .00125, 1000 warmup, cosine decay, weight decay .01 (Appendix F.3, Table 12). 2048 bytes vs 512 subwords target roughly similar text, not verified exact matching. Perceiver IO++ 425M/241B/4.2 steps/s/81.8 is a larger budget, not a matched-FLOP uplift. Image/video/audio/StarCraft results do not establish byte language generation or text retrieval fidelity.

### Latest returned-card finding (supersedes old discovery limits)

- **Current four units:** Model-specificsubwords / fullyfinetunedencoderor4-bitLoRAdecoder / tasklabels/spans / supervisedDI/TC/EQA; TP/IPPearsonassociations,notnativebytecausalintervention.
- **Fixed scope:** [R10/BIW-0134](../03_reading/R10/BIW-0134.md), FULL as declared in sourcecard; actual relevant passage read here.

Does a language's token-length disparity relative to English consistently predict performance on dialect tasks? The authors measure **tokenization parity (TP)**, the language/English ratio of tokenizer sequence lengths on parallel content, and **information parity (IP)**, English/language total negative-log-likelihood ratio under a model (§3.1, pp.23994–95); they correlate each with separately adapted task performance rather than presenting a new tokenizer. They use Pearson correlation, parallel FLORES sentences, script/resource groupings, full fine-tuning of BERT encoders, and 4-bit quantized low-rank adaptation (LoRA) for decoder models. These are observed associations across models/languages, not randomized causal tokenization interventions.

Input is model-specific subword units (WordPiece, byte-BPE or SentencePiece depending on model); encoder outputs dialect/topic labels or answer spans, decoder instruction tuning generates labels/spans. TP is relative sequence length for parallel sentences, not a score for the individual byte or an ordinal fairness guarantee. IP compares conditional sequence log-loss under a stated model and reference translation; it is not a measured semantic representation, a byte-normalized probability, or fairness itself. No native byte-step LM is trained.

Decoder SFT uses 4-bit quantization and LoRA rank 8 or 16, alpha 8, dropout 0.1, batch 1/2/4 with gradient accumulation 8, LR 2e-4 or 5e-5, with Optuna; encoder full fine-tuning uses 3 epochs, AdamW LR 2e-5, batch 8/16, weight decay 0.01 (§4.1). Appendix E reports A100/V100, ~4 hours–1.5 days for decoder experiments vs 1–2 hours for encoders. Number of GPUs, per-task full hyperparameters and pretraining budgets are not fully specified; this is not an equal-compute architecture comparison. The authors say encoders outperform decoders in all tasks, but their own Table 7 reports Korean EQA F1 0.10/0.092 for mBERT vs 0.482/0.500 Phi; such general language should be understood at reported aggregate level, not every cell.

Overall DI reverses the TP sign relative to TC/EQA for Phi and mBERT; Llama DI retains the expected negative sign. IP changes sign for Phi DI vs TC/EQA. The named table coefficients remain unchanged. R2 withdraws the earlier definite TP prose-conflict assertion: §5.2 first gives negative Llama TP, while a later positive sentence may refer to Llama IP (+0.268). Attribute each sign to TP or IP; an unambiguous TP contradiction is not established. The explanation that finer fragments help surface dialect discrimination is a hypothesis. It is not proof that fragmentation causes improved fairness.

Table 8's per-group Phi TC correlations vary from +0.873 (Latin-high) to −0.785 (Latin-low); Phi non-Latin-high IP is −0.862 whereas overall IP is +0.812. These group values are descriptive and should not be substituted for overall numbers. Per-correlation sample sizes and significance/uncertainty are not reported in Table 8; available task/language counts do not establish the effective paired n in each cell. No p-values are inferred.

§5.3/Figure 6 presents Llama-3.2 displayed fragments for Arabic and an example Devanagari character र with UTF-8 bytes `E0 A4 B0` shown as Latin-looking `à¤°` (§5.3, pp.23998–99). The authors themselves say byte sequences **may be reassembled** as proper Unicode on decoding. Displayed byte-mapped glyphs alone are not evidence that actual text was corrupted, lost, or irreversibly decoded; not all byte-level vocabularies use literal Latin-1 as their actual internal encoding. The exact tokenizer artifact, its byte-to-symbol mapping, per-token round trip and output error rates were not verified. The observation of fragmentation and the speculation about downstream harm must remain separate.

Fields absent in the read paper are **unreported**; runtime/code/prefix stability not examined is **unverified**; no further FULL is required merely to fill those fields.


**Full-scope dialect correction:** R10 full Appendix FTable 8/Figure5: DI TP r(Phi)=+.638,mBERT=+.4836,Llama=−.380; Phi DI IP=−.413. TC TP(Phi/Llama/mBERT)=−.683/−.716/−.605; EQA=−.834/−.528/−.938. Per-correlation pairedn and significance not reported. R2 correction: the later positive Llama sentence may refer to IP (+0.268), not TP (−0.380); the earlier definite TP-conflict attribution is withdrawn. §5.3 says bytes may be reassembled; Latin-like glyphs and absence as standalone vocab entries do not prove corruption/unrepresentability. DISCOVERY_CORRECTIONS T8 source-reading complete; R2 referent attribution now adopted, not a claim of equal adaptation or tokenizer causality.

**Final R2 / claim-rules adoption** ([CLAIM_RULES](../05_review/CLAIM_RULES.md); [FULL_READING_AUDIT_R2](../05_review/FULL_READING_AUDIT_R2.md)): Current R2 adoption — dialect TP and IP must be named separately. Appendix F Table 8 gives DI TP correlations +0.638 (Phi), +0.4836 (mBERT), −0.380 (Llama), and DI IP −0.413 (Phi), +0.268 (Llama). Section5.2 explicitly describes Llama TP as negative; the later positive sentence follows IP discussion and may refer to IP. The earlier definite “TP prose contradicts the table” assertion is withdrawn, not a confirmed source conflict. Coefficients and task-dependent associations are unchanged. Effective paired n/significance are not reported in Table8; no causal fairness or Unicode-corruption conclusion follows. Decoder4-bitLoRA and encoderfulltuning are different budgets. T8 whole-source reading is complete; runtime/tokenizer artifacts remain unverified.

<a id="BIP-0125"></a>
## BIP-0125 — Claiming universal raw-character processing can conceal language-specific normalization and weak noise evidence

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** DISCOVERY A/P only — not upgraded. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0054](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0054) — Character-level Convolutional Networks for Text Classification. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Claiming universal raw-character processing can conceal language-specific normalization and weak noise evidence.
- **One-sentence solution:** Test alphabet choices and expose the preprocessing and data-regime dependence of character CNN results.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **E:** alphabet/case ablation and synonym-based data augmentation; semantic invariance supplied through WordNet-derived thesaurus.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** Prescribed **70-character** one-hot alphabet / temporal CNN features / document class / class label. Out-of-alphabet and blank characters become zero; length 1014. Chinese Sogou is converted to Pinyin using segmentation/transliteration.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** Supervised classification; SGD, momentum, max pooling, dropout; complete document window, **not causal generation**.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** Sogou Chinese is segmented and converted to Pinyin; n-gram TFIDF remains strong up to several hundred thousand examples.
- **Limits:** Authors explicitly say better handling of exotic misspellings/emoticons was **not directly established**; replacing alphabet with bytes is A, not reported result. §2.4, §4 Sogou, §5 / P.

**Evidence ceiling:** no corresponding full card was found. Retain this original source-depth claim only; no upgrade is inferred from nearby papers. Further full reading is optional unless this claim becomes a synthesis pillar.

- **Source mapping (preserved):** [S01-R05](../01_discovery/S01/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 21).
- **Manual multi-label assignment:** [C01](TAXONOMY.md#C01), [C10](TAXONOMY.md#C10).

<a id="BIP-0126"></a>
## BIP-0126 — Pure pooling exposes orthographic features but adding a conventional MLP degrades downstream word modeling

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0055](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0055) — Character-Aware Neural Language Models. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Pure pooling exposes orthographic features but adding a conventional MLP degrades downstream word modeling.
- **One-sentence solution:** Insert highway gates that learn when to carry versus transform pooled spelling features.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **E:** highway carry/transform gates adaptively combine n-gram features; negative transform-bias initialization favors carry.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** Indexed characters inside presegmented words / CNN-max-highway word vectors and word-timeLSTM / fixed word vocabulary / next-wordCE; characteralphabet exact encoding unreported.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R02/BIW-0055](../03_reading/R02/BIW-0055.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R02/BIW-0055](../03_reading/R02/BIW-0055.md):** PTB input training ~1M word tokens / 10k words, large English 20M / 60k; other datasets and inventories Table 1. Architecture small/large: 15-d character embeddings; widths 1–6 / 1–7; two LSTM layers of 300 / 650; highway one/two layers (Table 2). Truncated backpropagation 35 **word steps**, SGD learning rate 1 halved on inadequate validation PPL improvement; batch 20/100, dropout 0.5, gradient norm ≤5; 25 epochs non-Arabic, 30 Arabic (Experimental Setup).
- PTB Table 3: small character 92.3 vs small word 97.6 PPL, each ~5M parameters; large character **78.9 / 19M** vs 85.4 / 20M word baseline and published LSTM-2 **78.4 / 52M**. The ≈60% saving is relative to the latter, not the authors' 20M word model.
- Table 4 DATA-S large models: Czech 371 vs word 493 vs morphology 398; German 239 vs 286 vs 263; Arabic **148 vs 172 vs 148**—a tie with morphology, not a strict win on every cell. DATA-L Table 5 character vs word: German 305 vs 347, English 216 vs 236; published morphological log-bilinear Russian **300** beats char **313**, so broad 'beats every morphology comparator' is false. Actual vocabularies, architectures and sizes differ; PPLs across different languages/tokenizations should not be compared as common byte probabilities.
- : Table 7 on small/large PTB: no highway **100.3/84.6**, one highway **92.3/79.7**, two **90.1/78.9**, ordinary one-layer MLP **111.2/92.6**. Authors suggest optimization difficulty rather than prove it; extra CNN layers did not help, combined word+character input gave 81 PPL (Further Observations). Nearest-neighbor/PCA analyses reveal orthographic and some semantic associations, not causal identification of morphemes; filters generally do not align with valid morphemes.
- : Fixed word output and local composition cost remain. Large PTB character model trained at **~1500 word tokens/s** vs word model **~3000/s**; precomputing all input-word compositions can match scoring speed at memory expense. All GPUs had 2GB memory; large DATA-L models were not trained due to memory. No GPU model, energy, matched-FLOPs or inference latency provided. No external teacher; no model-code execution.


**Remaining-field rule:** facts expressly absent in the read fixed paper/card are **unreported**, not a request to reread the paper. Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. Only reported conditions support this record.

<a id="BIP-0127"></a>
## BIP-0127 — Eliminating a word input lookup does not eliminate large-output-vocabulary cost or local composition overhead

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0055](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0055) — Character-Aware Neural Language Models. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Eliminating a word input lookup does not eliminate large-output-vocabulary cost or local composition overhead.
- **One-sentence solution:** Retain a word classifier, use hierarchical output softmax for large vocabularies and optionally cache composed inputs.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **E:** hierarchical softmax decomposes word probability; cached CNN features trade memory for scoring speed.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** Indexed characters inside presegmented words / CNN-max-highway word vectors and word-timeLSTM / fixed word vocabulary / next-wordCE; characteralphabet exact encoding unreported.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R02/BIW-0055](../03_reading/R02/BIW-0055.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R02/BIW-0055](../03_reading/R02/BIW-0055.md):** PTB input training ~1M word tokens / 10k words, large English 20M / 60k; other datasets and inventories Table 1. Architecture small/large: 15-d character embeddings; widths 1–6 / 1–7; two LSTM layers of 300 / 650; highway one/two layers (Table 2). Truncated backpropagation 35 **word steps**, SGD learning rate 1 halved on inadequate validation PPL improvement; batch 20/100, dropout 0.5, gradient norm ≤5; 25 epochs non-Arabic, 30 Arabic (Experimental Setup).
- PTB Table 3: small character 92.3 vs small word 97.6 PPL, each ~5M parameters; large character **78.9 / 19M** vs 85.4 / 20M word baseline and published LSTM-2 **78.4 / 52M**. The ≈60% saving is relative to the latter, not the authors' 20M word model.
- Table 4 DATA-S large models: Czech 371 vs word 493 vs morphology 398; German 239 vs 286 vs 263; Arabic **148 vs 172 vs 148**—a tie with morphology, not a strict win on every cell. DATA-L Table 5 character vs word: German 305 vs 347, English 216 vs 236; published morphological log-bilinear Russian **300** beats char **313**, so broad 'beats every morphology comparator' is false. Actual vocabularies, architectures and sizes differ; PPLs across different languages/tokenizations should not be compared as common byte probabilities.
- : Table 7 on small/large PTB: no highway **100.3/84.6**, one highway **92.3/79.7**, two **90.1/78.9**, ordinary one-layer MLP **111.2/92.6**. Authors suggest optimization difficulty rather than prove it; extra CNN layers did not help, combined word+character input gave 81 PPL (Further Observations). Nearest-neighbor/PCA analyses reveal orthographic and some semantic associations, not causal identification of morphemes; filters generally do not align with valid morphemes.
- : Fixed word output and local composition cost remain. Large PTB character model trained at **~1500 word tokens/s** vs word model **~3000/s**; precomputing all input-word compositions can match scoring speed at memory expense. All GPUs had 2GB memory; large DATA-L models were not trained due to memory. No GPU model, energy, matched-FLOPs or inference latency provided. No external teacher; no model-code execution.

Only reported conditions support this record.

<a id="BIP-0129"></a>
## BIP-0129 — Language-specific tokenization pipelines prevent sharing one compact raw-text annotation model across scripts

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0057](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0057) — Multilingual Language Processing From Bytes. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Language-specific tokenization pipelines prevent sharing one compact raw-text annotation model across scripts.
- **One-sentence solution:** Encode raw UTF-8 bytes and decode annotation components rather than preprocessing words.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **E:** stacked LSTM sequence-to-sequence model maps complete segment to serialized start/length/label outputs.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** UTF-8bytes+GO/DROP in60byte windows / same recurrentLSTM parameters in input/output phases / start,length,label events+STOP / annotation conditional likelihood, not next textbyte.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R02/BIW-0057](../03_reading/R02/BIW-0057.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R02/BIW-0057](../03_reading/R02/BIW-0057.md):** language-specific tokenization and processing pipelines hinder a compact cross-script annotator. **Solution:** read UTF-8 byte windows with a shared LSTM and train one model on all languages for each task. Input includes 256 byte values, GO and DROP; windows can split multibyte Unicode characters (§§1, 3.1–3.2). No Unicode normalization policy specified. Representations are continuous LSTM states; output is **span annotations**, not text bytes.
- : cross-product classification over all possible start/length/label triples is large and rigid. **Solution:** autoregressively serialize each annotation as separate `start, length, label` events followed by STOP. The same softmax covers all start positions, lengths, labels and STOP; each prediction may choose any event type. Invalid or incomplete spans are rare and ignored, not formally precluded (§3.1). No independent verifier or enforcement is described. Greedy argmax feeds prior outputs back; beam search improved <0.2 absolute (§5).
- : local-string memorization and independently segmented windows hurt generalization and cross-boundary spans. **Solution:** randomly replace input bytes with DROP without changing labels and overlap inference windows (§§4–5). Train 60-byte windows at one-byte shifts, ignore training spans not fully contained. At inference use 60-byte windows overlapped by 30 bytes, retain last 30-byte predictions except initial window as described; overlap adds roughly twice the input processing on long texts and does not mathematically guarantee coverage of arbitrarily long spans. Handling of retained crossing spans is not fully specified.


**Remaining-field rule:** facts expressly absent in the read fixed paper/card are **unreported**, not a request to reread the paper. Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. Only reported conditions support this record.

## BIP-0132 — Character seq2seq recurrence or pooled attention can be expensive and demand extensive state memorization

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.

- **Specific problem:** Character seq2seq recurrence or pooled attention can be expensive and demand extensive state memorization.
- **One-sentence solution:** Use resolution-preserving dilated convolutional encoders and decoders.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Dilated one-dimensional causal target convolutions, unmasked source convolutions, residual multiplicative/ReLU blocks and layer normalization; dynamic source unfolding and EOS-terminated beam search. LM and MT use distinct alphabets; not an unexamined byte-name inference.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** Hutter90M/5M/5Mbyte splits with205observedsymbols; MT296English/323Germancharacters / dilated convolution states / next benchmark symbol or targetcharacter+EOS / causalLM or conditionaltranslation likelihood.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R02/BIW-0058](../03_reading/R02/BIW-0058.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R02/BIW-0058](../03_reading/R02/BIW-0058.md):** recurrent seq2seq decoders are serial in training, fixed-vector encoders compress source information, and all-pairs attention incurs length-dependent cost. **Solution:** stack a resolution-preserving dilated convolutional source encoder with a causally masked dilated convolutional target decoder, dynamically unfold until EOS (§§2–4, Figs. 1–3). Dilations expand receptive field quickly; residual blocks ease deep optimization, layer normalization avoids computing statistics across future target positions. Unlike dense attention, each decoder position has finite reachable source/target context, determined by convolution depth and dilation; source encoder is unmasked so can use surrounding source positions. It is not an online source-streaming translation guarantee.


**Remaining-field rule:** facts expressly absent in the read fixed paper/card are **unreported**, not a request to reread the paper. Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. Only reported conditions support this record.

<a id="BIP-0136"></a>
## BIP-0136 — General-domain wordpieces oversegment domain terminology and destabilize word-level representation

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0066](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0066) — CharacterBERT: Reconciling ELMo and BERT for Word-Level Open-Vocabulary Representations From Characters. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** General-domain wordpieces oversegment domain terminology and destabilize word-level representation.
- **One-sentence solution:** Construct one word-position vector from local UTF-8 byte CNN features instead of splitting into wordpieces.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **E:** ELMo-style local byte CNN, max pooling, two highway layers, projection to768; BERT contextualizes word positions.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** UTF-8 bytes inside externally segmented word tokens,263entries and localcap50 / CNN-highway word vectors+BERT word positions / task heads or temporary100Kword classifier / whole-wordMLM+NSP; outside100Knevermasked.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R01/BIW-0066](../03_reading/R01/BIW-0066.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R01/BIW-0066](../03_reading/R01/BIW-0066.md):** Problem: general-domain WordPiece over-fragments specialized terminology. Solution: retain externally supplied word units but compose each from UTF-8 bytes with an ELMo-style CNN. On 1M medical tokens, ~13% of occurrences are whole in a medical vocabulary yet split by the general vocabulary (Figure 1, §2); this statistic alone does not demonstrate downstream causation. Example `choledocholithiasis`: 2 medical vs 7 general pieces (Table 1).
Problem: open inputs and open targets are easily conflated. Solution: fixed 100k frequent word classifier limits the MLM prediction problem while allowing byte-composed input representations. Rare words receive no direct masking targets, although can appear as context. Since word positions are presegmented and 50-local-unit capped, neither unrestricted arbitrary raw text handling nor unlimited rare word recovery follows.
Under matched pretraining recipes, medical CharacterBERT's nine-model ensembles improve over medical BERT roughly 1.5 ChemProt F1, 2 DDI F1, 0.5 MEDNLI/i2b2 points (§5.4, Figure 5); visually checked Appendix Figure 8 ensemble medians are 75.40 vs 73.94 ChemProt, 82.74 vs 80.20 DDI, 85.97 vs 85.65 MedNLI accuracy, 89.75 vs 89.51 i2b2 F1. **ClinicalSTS reverses**: 85.62 vs 86.08 Pearson ensemble median, with unstable single-model results and only 600 training examples. Do not generalize the medical gains to every task. Noise Figure 7 evaluates deletion/addition/replacement/swap per token; at 40% test-only noise the paper describes ~5-point advantage (the plot axis is accuracy although §5.5 calls it F1). Gains combine representation, output objective, preprocessing and training costs; not a CNN-only causal ablation.


**Remaining-field rule:** facts expressly absent in the read fixed paper/card are **unreported**, not a request to reread the paper. Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. Only reported conditions support this record.

- **Manual multi-label assignment:** [C02](TAXONOMY.md#C02).

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R01/BIW-0066](../03_reading/R01/BIW-0066.md):** Problem: general-domain WordPiece over-fragments specialized terminology. Solution: retain externally supplied word units but compose each from UTF-8 bytes with an ELMo-style CNN. On 1M medical tokens, ~13% of occurrences are whole in a medical vocabulary yet split by the general vocabulary (Figure 1, §2); this statistic alone does not demonstrate downstream causation. Example `choledocholithiasis`: 2 medical vs 7 general pieces (Table 1).
Problem: open inputs and open targets are easily conflated. Solution: fixed 100k frequent word classifier limits the MLM prediction problem while allowing byte-composed input representations. Rare words receive no direct masking targets, although can appear as context. Since word positions are presegmented and 50-local-unit capped, neither unrestricted arbitrary raw text handling nor unlimited rare word recovery follows.
Under matched pretraining recipes, medical CharacterBERT's nine-model ensembles improve over medical BERT roughly 1.5 ChemProt F1, 2 DDI F1, 0.5 MEDNLI/i2b2 points (§5.4, Figure 5); visually checked Appendix Figure 8 ensemble medians are 75.40 vs 73.94 ChemProt, 82.74 vs 80.20 DDI, 85.97 vs 85.65 MedNLI accuracy, 89.75 vs 89.51 i2b2 F1. **ClinicalSTS reverses**: 85.62 vs 86.08 Pearson ensemble median, with unstable single-model results and only 600 training examples. Do not generalize the medical gains to every task. Noise Figure 7 evaluates deletion/addition/replacement/swap per token; at 40% test-only noise the paper describes ~5-point advantage (the plot axis is accuracy although §5.5 calls it F1). Gains combine representation, output objective, preprocessing and training costs; not a CNN-only causal ablation.

## BIP-0139 — Apparent gains from removing embeddings may actually arise from changing how decoder dropout corrupts teacher-forced inputs

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0068](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0068) — Neural Machine Translation without Embeddings. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Apparent gains from removing embeddings may actually arise from changing how decoder dropout corrupts teacher-forced inputs.
- **One-sentence solution:** Control decoder token dropout across all tokenization and embedding variants.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **E:** decoder-input token dropout regularizes prefix conditioning and separates optimization from architecture.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** UTF-8 source/target bytes / Transformer byte positions from fixed one-hot coordinates / softmax_d coordinate logits (special/unused-coordinate treatment unreported) / teacher-forced translationCE+label smoothing.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R01/BIW-0068](../03_reading/R01/BIW-0068.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R01/BIW-0068](../03_reading/R01/BIW-0068.md):** Problem: learned byte embedding tables are conventional but their benefit is unclear when alphabet size < hidden width. Solution: replace the shared learned input/output lookup and unembedding with fixed one-hot coordinates and predict by direct hidden-coordinate softmax. With ordinary baseline recipe Table 2 finds higher BLEU without embeddings in 19/20 directions, tie ru→en, ~+0.5 average; e.g. en→zh 21.0 vs embedded-byte 20.2; ja→en 12.2 vs 11.4. This apparent gain is confounded: elementwise decoder-input dropout deletes the entire fixed one-hot token but only coordinates of a dense learned embedding (§6).
Problem: tokenization changes the semantics of standard dropout. Solution: test explicit decoder-side token dropout p=.2 on embedding-based controls and allow tuning it. Table 3 mean validation gains on xx→en: +0.92 BLEU learned-byte, +0.83 fixed-byte; 7/160 validation conditions decrease. Under tuned token dropout Table 4 reverses headline interpretation: en→xx learned vs fixed bytes nearly equal; xx→en fixed is on average 0.45 BLEU worse, while subword exceeds the next best by 0.76. Example ja→en learned byte 12.3 vs fixed 11.2; ru→en 22.5 vs 22.0. Thus removing learned embedding is not independently demonstrated beneficial after the optimization control. The authors' exposure-bias explanation is a hypothesis.

Only reported conditions support this record.

### Latest returned-card finding (supersedes old discovery limits)

- **Current four units:** UTF-8byte stream of pretokenized/shuffled lm1b withUNKsubstitutions / full512byte Transformer positions / 256next-byte classes / causal byteCE; convertedwordPPL uses sameprocessedcorpus counts.
- **Fixed scope:** [R09/BIW-0071](../03_reading/R09/BIW-0071.md), FULL as declared in sourcecard; actual relevant passage read here.

: the apparent large-data word/character performance gap need not imply tokenization is intrinsically required. Their proposed remedy is a larger *plain* 40-layer causal Transformer, not pooling, learned segmentation, external boundary teacher or a new objective. UTF-8 byte input and next-byte supervision use one position per byte internally and a 256-way next-byte output (§2). A 512-byte window is sampled across sentence boundaries; 16 heads, d=1024, FFN=8192, ~836M total parameters including ~66K byte embeddings. The attention mask ensures a representation after byte i predicts i+1, not future bytes; no recurrence is used. Whether the input/output matrices are tied, EOS/invalid UTF-8 policy and generation/cache implementation are unreported.

Training uses Adam initial 1e-4, geometric decay .99 each 10k steps, 2M steps, batch 1024, dropout .3 (§2.1). This is 2M × 1024 × 512 ≈1.05 trillion sampled byte positions, **not** unique corpus bytes; training corpus is 4,132,763,660 bytes. Accelerator model, wall time and total training FLOPs are unreported. No claim of matched wall-clock/compute against word baselines follows.

Table 2 reports this ~0.8B byte model at 0.874 BPB / 23.0 word PPL, versus previous 0.2B byte T64 1.033 / 40.6; cited word or wordpiece systems range 21.8–28.0, including Transformer-XL word model 0.8B/21.8, a 1.0B word model at 23.0 and a 4.9B wordpiece model at 24.0. The [versioned HTML Table 2](https://arxiv.org/html/1908.10322v1) was consulted because the PDF text extraction interleaves the rows. These are literature comparisons, not controlled architecture/compute experiments. Test PPL equality at 23.0 does not prove equal real-world tokenizer-free deployment costs.

Fields absent in the read paper are **unreported**; runtime/code/prefix stability not examined is **unverified**; no further FULL is required merely to fill those fields.

### Latest returned-card finding (supersedes old discovery limits)

- **Current four units:** UTF-8byte stream of pretokenized/shuffled lm1b withUNKsubstitutions / full512byte Transformer positions / 256next-byte classes / causal byteCE; convertedwordPPL uses sameprocessedcorpus counts.
- **Fixed scope:** [R09/BIW-0071](../03_reading/R09/BIW-0071.md), FULL as declared in sourcecard; actual relevant passage read here.

The lm1b benchmark is a pretokenized, sentence-shuffled word corpus with rare words replaced by UNK (§3.1). No additional tokenizer is applied to its byte stream, but the *underlying data are not raw, untouched original text*. Spaces/newlines and literal UNK text remain observable. Table 1 counts 798,947,561 training word events, 4,132,763,660 bytes; test 159,658 word events including EOS and 826,189 bytes including newlines. 95% of training sentences are shorter than 256 bytes and 99.78% below 512: it is not a strong long-document context test.

: for the **same scored processed corpus and matching event counts**, convert the native byte-chain score by PPL_word = 2^(BPB × 826189/159658). This merely re-expresses that path's total log likelihood per word event; it does not equate a subword canonical-path probability with an arbitrary marginalized string probability, nor repair incompatible EOS/newline accounting. The paper's notation that information is segmentation-independent is conditional on a common probability event, not a theorem that separately trained models assign it equal mass.

Scoring from scratch at stride 1 maximizes available 512-byte context and is used for final test. For development, stride 256 scores the second half of each overlapping window in parallel, with contexts varying by position: dev 0.874055 BPB at stride 1 versus 0.87413 at 256 (§2.2). This is scoring acceleration, not cached sequential generation throughput.

Fields absent in the read paper are **unreported**; runtime/code/prefix stability not examined is **unverified**; no further FULL is required merely to fill those fields.

## BIP-0144 — Unsegmented text offers no directly observed lexical units

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0043](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0043) — Unsupervised Learning of Word Boundary with Description Length Gain. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Unsegmented text offers no directly observed lexical units.
- **One-sentence solution:** Select the utterance segmentation maximizing description-length gain of its component segments.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Non-neural substring frequency counts, empirical Shannon–Fano description lengths and Viterbi-style segmentation DP. EM and hierarchical chunking are future work, not implemented neural techniques.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** Corpuscharacter/symbol strings (spaces visible ordinarysymbols) / indexedsubstringcounts and DPsegments / boundaries/segments / unsuperviseddescription-lengthgain, non-neural.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R02/BIW-0043](../03_reading/R02/BIW-0043.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R02/BIW-0043](../03_reading/R02/BIW-0043.md):** Unknown word boundaries and unknown words make reliance on a fixed dictionary and delimiters inadequate. **Solution:** count substrings in a corpus, score their description-length gain, and dynamically choose a flat segmentation maximizing a corpus-derived gain score (§§1–3).
- This is a **non-neural** historical minimum-description-length/statistical segmentation method, not a trained byte Transformer. Shannon–Fano empirical code length from corpus symbol frequencies provides the scoring criterion; a dictionary-rule replacement accounts for storing a candidate substring once and replacing its occurrences with an index; a Viterbi-style dynamic program searches segmentations. Expected-maximization and hierarchical chunking are only future work (§5).
- Input is a character/symbol sequence with corpus-wide n-gram counts, not a specified UTF-8 byte stream; representation is indexed string candidates; output is a sequence of segments/boundaries, and there are **no learned neural readout heads**. Training supervision is unlabeled corpus counts; whitespace is used for external evaluation, not supplied as boundary labels, although spaces **are present as ordinary characters to the learner** (§4). Lowercasing and replacing full stops by `@` are described for the example; exact encoding/alphabet and any global normalization beyond what is stated are unknown.
- Entire corpus and the whole utterance are available for candidate counts and decoding; there is no causal streaming-generation claim, teacher, next-byte distribution, EOS policy, verifier, or head-sharing question.


**Remaining-field rule:** facts expressly absent in the read fixed paper/card are **unreported**, not a request to reread the paper. Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. Only reported conditions support this record.

## BIP-0147 — Unlabelled Chinese sentences lack a single gold segmentation to train a segment-generating model

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.

- **Specific problem:** Unlabelled Chinese sentences lack a single gold segmentation to train a segment-generating model.
- **One-sentence solution:** Maximize sentence likelihood summed over candidate segmentations and recover the best segmentation by dynamic programming.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Context LSTM initializes a segment-decoder LSTM; segment-end symbols terminate units; bounded-length forward DP sums probabilities, Viterbi-style DP finds the maximum.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** Chinese characters → latent character segments → characters plus segment-end; marginal sentence likelihood. Generative segment decoder uses past context, while best posterior segmentation of observed text uses the full sentence.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** Chinese characters → latent character segments → characters plus segment-end; marginal sentence likelihood. Generative segment decoder uses past context, while best posterior segmentation of observed text uses the full sentence.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** Equations4–9; K=2/3/4; table1 PKU80.2/79.8/79.2 F1, showing larger maximum segments are not uniformly better. “Linear” algorithm statement is conditional on bounded K and segment scoring. ## BIP-0151 — Maintaining full subword resolution in every layer wastes computation on sequence-level tasks

<a id="BIP-0152"></a>
## BIP-0152 — Plain means lose within-block order and strided enumeration misses offset substrings

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0005](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0005) — Charformer: Fast Character Transformers via Gradient-based Subword Tokenization. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Plain means lose within-block order and strided enumeration misses offset substrings.
- **One-sentence solution:** Precede block averaging with convolution, with explicit offset enumeration as a costlier alternative.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** 1-D convolution contextualizes neighboring positions and supplies order-sensitive information; optional self-attention-like calibration couples block scores.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** UTF-8 bytes / candidate block soft mixtures then fixed-stride pooled states / autoregressive byte/sentinel sequences / span denoising, mean20byte spans.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R01/BIW-0005](../03_reading/R01/BIW-0005.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R01/BIW-0005](../03_reading/R01/BIW-0005.md):** GBST enumerates non-overlapping candidate blocks for each size b=1…M, mean-pools each, linearly scores, repeats each representation/score back across its b original byte positions, softmaxes over competing sizes per position and computes a weighted representation; a final fixed-stride mean pool sets compression (§2.1.1–2.1.5, Figure 2). The main setup uses a width-5 pre-GBST 1-D convolution rather than expensive enumeration of offset grids; convolution incorporates local ordering/context absent from simple bag means. Optional score calibration uses global score-by-score attention, permitting information from all positions; disabled on multilingual experiments. These are soft preferences, not a coherent sampled segmentation. Figure 3 is a single English example, not boundary ground truth. The simplified Appendix §7.4 uses `range(1, max_subword_block_width)` with default 4 (thus 1–3), while the conceptual description and Figure 3 discuss widths 1–4: it is illustrative code, so actual experiments' inclusion of width 4 requires separate source/config verification.

**[R01/BIW-0005](../03_reading/R01/BIW-0005.md):** Problem: fixed tokenization gives rigid segmentation and byte attention is expensive. Solution: learn candidate byte-block mixtures under the downstream denoising objective before fixed-rate reduction. On TyDiQA-GoldP at matched ds=4, small GBST F1 66.6 vs local-attention/strided-convolution 64.9; base 73.2 vs 70.6 (Table 7, §4.3). The paper accidentally cites Table 9 there; Table 9 is the 1.23B experiment. Raising ds from 2 to 4 worsens base 75.8→73.2. Offset enumeration did not consistently beat convolution (Table 8).
Problem: total model parameters hide compute redistribution. Solution: deep/narrow encoder-heavy SBase (24 encoder/6 decoder layers, 134M) rather than the 203M base. On English GLUE average SBase 83.6 vs byte T5-SBase 82.6 and subword T5 84.3; unscaled Charformer 81.4 vs byte T5 81.5 (Table 1)—not an across-task win. Table 6: 16 TPUv3, batch 64, 1024-byte inputs, ds=3, SBase 20 steps/s, 8.7e12 forward FLOPs, 1.34 GB peak/device versus byte T5 8.2, 2.9e13, 3.09 GB. T5 subword row is 512 tokens at 9.3 steps/s; unequal raw contexts and architecture preclude a universal speedup.
Multilingual mC4: mT5 582M vs Charformer SBase 134M; Table 5 gives 1.54 vs 1.98 steps/s for 64 TPUv3 at batch 1024; mT5 L=1024 subword, Charformer L=2048 byte and ds=2; long-PT batch 2048 is 1.01 steps/s. Equal compressed-position exposure vs roughly equal original text are different arms; sentencepiece ≈4.1 bytes/token is an estimate, not exact alignment. F1 on multilingual TyDiQA 80.8 mT5 vs 81.2 long-PT, but zero-shot XNLI 75.4 vs 67.8 (Table 4), and byte T5 base was pretrained at 1024 rather than 2048 due to cost. Fine-tuning froze GBST for XNLI/PAWS-X; Table 16 freezing can harm XNLI at some strides. Calibration did not help multilingual. At 1.23B, Charformer 86.3 vs ByT5 87.7 F1 with ~100k fewer training steps (Appendix §7.2, Table 9).
Social-media classification is not synthetic typo proof: Wiki Comments accuracy Charformer Base 92.7 vs byte T5 93.2, despite higher AUC-PR 79.7 vs 75.4 (Table 2); claims must name metric. Nonconcatenative morphology and stable causal online operation remain untested.


**Central correction (P1-06; v3 now read; [correction source](../05_review/DISCOVERY_CORRECTIONS.md)):** R01 reads v3 whole method/results/appendix: soft candidate mixtures then fixed downsampling; optional global score calibration is non-prefix and disabled multilingual. Prior v2 fragments remain historical; exhaustive v2→v3 diff unverified. Appendix illustrative range excludes upper bound4, conceptual method uses1–4; actual experimental config unverified, not an occasion for repeated FULL.

**Remaining-field rule:** facts expressly absent in the read fixed paper/card are **unreported**, not a request to reread the paper. Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. Only reported conditions support this record.

- **Manual multi-label assignment:** [C02](TAXONOMY.md#C02).

## BIP-0153 — An unordered weighted byte pool could give the same result for different byte orders

- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R01/BIW-0006](../03_reading/R01/BIW-0006.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R01/BIW-0006](../03_reading/R01/BIW-0006.md):** UTF-8 bytes plus span sentinels form the encoder input; a sliding-window local Transformer predicts a Bernoulli frontier probability for every byte. The cumulative frontier count defines a Poisson-binomial block-index distribution; a truncated Gaussian with matched mean/variance approximates byte-to-block membership (§3.1.1–2). Weighted byte embeddings are processed by a depthwise 1-D convolution and max pooled per block, making composition order-sensitive, then linearly projected to the T5 encoder width (§3.1.3, Appendix D). The retained block sequence is truncated to `min(LB,L/4)`, incentivizing fewer blocks; it is a hard capacity constraint, not merely an LM objective. Rounded expected block indices are used for post-hoc visualization; soft assignments are actually used during training (§6.2). Extra eligible block representations beyond the cap are discarded, so absence of text loss cannot be assumed. Appendix A caches kernel-times-byte products shared across block slots for computational savings; this is an intermediate compute cache, not an autoregressive KV cache.


**Central correction (P1-06; metadata and evidence refinement; [correction source](../05_review/DISCOVERY_CORRECTIONS.md)):** R01 confirms authors Nathan Godey, Roman Castagné, Éric de la Clergerie, Benoît Sagot; Gaussian soft assignment, order-sensitive depthwise CNN/max pooling, hardL/4 truncation and autoregressive byte decoder. No-truncation degeneration is qualitative, not a missing quantified table to invent. Clean-to-noisy separation is weak without adaptation;2.61/9.06s train steps is not decode latency.

**Remaining-field rule:** facts expressly absent in the read fixed paper/card are **unreported**, not a request to reread the paper. Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. Only reported conditions support this record.

## BIP-0154 — Optimizing denoising alone often learns one block per byte rather than useful compression

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0006](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0006) — MANTa: Efficient Gradient-Based Tokenization for Robust End-to-End Language Modeling. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Optimizing denoising alone often learns one block per byte rather than useful compression.
- **One-sentence solution:** Truncate the block sequence to at most one quarter of the input length so fitting all input information incentivizes longer blocks.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Hard length bottleneck supplies pressure in addition to task gradients; separate smaller tokenizer learning rate stabilizes training.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** UTF-8 bytes / Gaussian soft byte-to-block assignment, depthwiseCNN/max, retained≤L/4blocks / autoregressive byte/sentinel targets / span denoising; hard length bottleneck, not task loss alone.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R01/BIW-0006](../03_reading/R01/BIW-0006.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R01/BIW-0006](../03_reading/R01/BIW-0006.md):** For rigid vocabulary and expensive fine-grained encoding, learn local frontier probabilities jointly with byte denoising, approximate block membership and feed order-sensitive soft pooled representations to a compressed encoder. Without the `L/4` bottleneck, §6.1 reports the block count often degenerates to approximately one per byte, hurting speed and eventual quality; the paper provides no quantified matched ablation. Gaussian assignment is not an exact sum over segmentations, nor proof that discovered segments are linguistic words.
Adapt to unfamiliar domains/noise by allowing segmentation to update during fine-tuning. MedNLI accuracy: 57M MANTa-Small 75.6 vs T5-Small 75.3; 125M CharacterBERT 77.9 and BERT 77.7 use different corpora/model allocation (Table 3). Toxic comments: 200M MANTa 93.2 vs Charformer 92.7 and T5 91.5, latter results external (Table 4). Synthetic SST-2 Figure 3: deleting/replacing/inserting random bytes at 5/10/15%, clean-trained models are similarly degraded; when fine-tuned on noisy data MANTa and ByT5 are better retained than T5. This is not evidence of broad clean-to-noisy superiority, multilingual robustness or a causal segmentation-only gain.
Training speed is controlled separately from text exposure. Table 5: 16 V100, batch 1024, 1024 bytes vs 256 subword tokens, MANTa 2.61 s/step, 57M byte T5 9.06, 60M T5 1.13; ≈3.47× rather than exactly 4× faster than that byte baseline and 2.31× slower than subword. Not a decoding latency measurement. Model's Limitations expressly says byte-by-byte decoding adds generation cost. Small scaled ByT5 has a different architecture and is trained 200k steps at batch 64 under a same-training-time budget; MANTa/T5 train 65k at batch 1024, so these are not same-byte comparisons. MANTa 65k×1024 sequences at L=1024/2048 versus prior Charformer 1M×64 has roughly comparable nominal input positions, not exactly matched original text.
GLUE dev small: MANTa 77.1 vs T5 76.6; base 80.3 vs Charformer 81.4 and T5 84.3, different training batches/cited experiments (Tables 1–2). Appendix C test average 78.7 is a separate test result, not dev. English only; hyperparameter search limited (§6.4).


**Central correction (P1-06; metadata and evidence refinement; [correction source](../05_review/DISCOVERY_CORRECTIONS.md)):** R01 confirms authors Nathan Godey, Roman Castagné, Éric de la Clergerie, Benoît Sagot; Gaussian soft assignment, order-sensitive depthwise CNN/max pooling, hardL/4 truncation and autoregressive byte decoder. No-truncation degeneration is qualitative, not a missing quantified table to invent. Clean-to-noisy separation is weak without adaptation;2.61/9.06s train steps is not decode latency.

**Remaining-field rule:** facts expressly absent in the read fixed paper/card are **unreported**, not a request to reread the paper. Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. Only reported conditions support this record.

## BIP-0156 — Implicit task gradients may not provide a clear target for which positions deserve a new global update

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.

- **Specific problem:** Implicit task gradients may not provide a clear target for which positions deserve a new global update.
- **One-sentence solution:** Regress boundary probability toward one minus the current model’s probability of the observed next byte, with stop-gradient through that target.

Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** Bytes → boundary states → next bytes; LM + ratio + stop-gradient next-byte-confidence boundary loss. Prefix-causal policy; training targets know the next byte.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** Bytes → boundary states → next bytes; LM + ratio + stop-gradient next-byte-confidence boundary loss. Prefix-causal policy; training targets know the next byte.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** Matched~5×target/1.95GFLOPs per byte/50ksteps/839Bbytes: H-Net0.6701→smoothing0.6571; sigmoid0.6578; +CAB0.6568BPB. Most gain in this ladder is not CAB alone. Training targets use next byte; deployed policy still prefix-only.
- **Limits:** Specific unknowns and negative controls are retained in the evidence field.

## BIP-0160 — Pruning tokens discards potentially useful content and dynamic token counts complicate batching

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.

- **Learning / causal permissions:** Image/video/audio patch tokens → similarity-merged tokens → task labels; pretrained features, optional task fine-tuning. Noncausal vision matching; **not text/byte evidence**.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** MAE ViT-L,r8:matching84.25%/182.9images/s versus random pruning79.22%/184.4; original85.96%/93.3 onV100fp32/optimizedbatch. Noncontiguous, noncausal visual matching cannot be imported as a language causal segmentation result.

## BIP-0162 — Entropy peaks can miss newly computed results whose local format is predictable

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** REUSED-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0030](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0030) — Patch where the text is new: a compression view of where byte-level models should spend compute. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Entropy peaks can miss newly computed results whose local format is predictable.
- **One-sentence solution:** Start patches where a learned lookup table predicts that upcoming text is unlikely to repeat recent context.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** LZ77-inspired longest-repeat statistic within128bytes, capped16, supplies labels; empirical averages by prior-two-byte context form the rule with rare-context backoff.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** Bytes → novelty-rule patches → bytes; future-repeat labels estimated offline, table keyed by past bytes at deployment. LZ77-motivated novelty, not entropy or direct utility.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** Bytes → novelty-rule patches → bytes; future-repeat labels estimated offline, table keyed by past bytes at deployment. LZ77-motivated novelty, not entropy or direct utility.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** At~11%rate/50M/three seeds, computed values57.5 versus20.7%; finalanswers89.5 versus59.9%. Teacher-free does not mean supervision-free: offline target uses future training text. True-prefix completion, not unrestricted solution generation; same author/pipeline as W0357.
- **Limits:** Specific unknowns and negative controls are retained in the evidence field.
- **Carrying scoped FULL card(s), actually read in this integration:** [old scoped FULL/BIW-0030](../../flued_multigranularity_survey_20261108/03_reading/B14/W0358.md). The source locators and numerical conditions in the retained evidence above are carried by these cards; no new FULL credited.
