<a id="BIP-0268"></a>
## BIP-0268 — Fewer symbols might be mistaken for a complete explanation of good tokenization

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0131](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0131) — Tokenization Is More Than Compression. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Fewer symbols might be mistaken for a complete explanation of good tokenization
- **One-sentence solution:** construct minimum-token-count PathPiece segmentation and test whether its maximal compression improves models.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **E:** shortest/minimum segmentation over fixed vocabulary is the intervention; LM pretraining and downstream tests evaluate it. **A:** not proof compression never helps.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** Byte-completeBPE/unigram/PathPieceSUBWORDS / offline-segmentedcausalpositions / nextsubword / tokenCE; DPminimizestokencountforfixedvocabulary, notneural byte boundarylearning.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R08/BIW-0131](../03_reading/R08/BIW-0131.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R08/BIW-0131](../03_reading/R08/BIW-0131.md):** **:** On 10 English 5-shot multiple-choice tasks, not open-ended generation, Appendix G Table 11 gives no-pretokenization PathPieceR 40,960: 1.26B corpus tokens and 44.0% average; BPE merge 1.49B and 50.0%. Globally Pearson correlation of token count with accuracy is +0.241 (Table 2): shorter is not a sufficient general quality criterion, not evidence that computational compression lacks benefit. Equal token training and tokenizer differences confound both data exposure and computation. Top five methods were not individually significantly inferior to all others under the authors’ one-sided signed-rank testing; 30 task-by-vocabulary observations are not 30 independent training seeds (§5.2).
- **:** At 40,960, same BPE vocabulary with merge/greedy/PathPieceL yields 50.0/49.1/46.7% (Appendix E Fig. 8, Table 6); Unigram likelihood/greedy/PathPieceL 49.1/48.5/43.1% at this size (Table 6). Thus changing only inference segmentation can reverse compression-derived expectations. Initial BPE is better than initial Unigram or n-gram for PathPieceL (p≤0.01, §6.3); none vs FirstSpaceDigit vs SpaceDigit is not pure one-variable control because digit pre-tokenization is also present in the latter two. Space-separated and nonspace-delimited languages cannot be generalized from English.
- Appendix F: with BPE initialization RandTrain+greedy 48.596 versus SaGe 49.154, p=.0645; no significant SaGe improvement. PathPieceL+BPE 49.373 versus RandTrain+PathPieceL 46.46, p=.0137; poorly performing RandTrain+PathPieceL for n-gram initialization limits other comparisons. Digit constraint hurts SaGe n-gram in one test (p=.025) but is not significant in another (p=.54).
- At 40,960, BPE/PathPieceL-BPE/SaGe-BPE/Unigram give 50.0/49.4/49.2/49.1% at 350M, 53.1/49.2/52.2/52.4% at 1.3B, 54.2/52.7/55.0/54.7% at 2.4B (Table 14). An anomalous 1.3B 100k checkpoint is acknowledged (§ limitations, Fig. 7), so ranking reversals and significance are not definitive cross-scale laws.


**Remaining-field rule:** facts expressly absent in the read fixed paper/card are **unreported**, not a request to reread the paper. Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. Only reported conditions support this record.

- **Source mapping (preserved):** [S08-R015](../01_discovery/S08/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 34).
- **Manual multi-label assignment:** [C03](TAXONOMY.md#C03).

<a id="BIP-0270"></a>
## BIP-0270 — Subword models measure distances in compressed symbol units, unlike byte models

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0108](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0108) — Decoupling the Benefits of Subword Tokenization for Language Model Training via Byte-level Simulation. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Subword models measure distances in compressed symbol units, unlike byte models
- **One-sentence solution:** repeat subword-position indices across constituent byte positions and test both retained and withdrawn positional priors.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **E:** RoPE-position reindexing and temporary positional-prior curriculum. **A:** not an architecture-level semantic-distance oracle.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** UTF-8bytes (paper512vocab,specialIDsmasksunreported) andexternalBPEhints / byteorinitial4byte-sumpositions / byte,temporarilynextsubword / byteCEwithseparatecapacity/throughput/boundary/position/normalization/targetinterventions.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R08/BIW-0108](../03_reading/R08/BIW-0108.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R08/BIW-0108](../03_reading/R08/BIW-0108.md):** ** / capacity:** use Engram-inspired multihead input n-gram lookup as a capacity intervention, not a change in output alphabet: max n=3, eight heads, base 15k buckets/order, 71,065,088 added parameters (§5.1, Table 2). Figure 1 shows a small byte-loss improvement at 1.7B, Figure 7a a larger gap at 68M. No full embedding-capacity factorial or tied-vs-untied ablation.
- ** / throughput:** sum each consecutive four byte embeddings into one latent position, predict only the first byte of the *next* group for 50k steps then return to ordinary byte training (§5.2, Fig. 2). The first 50k stage suppresses 3/4 targets and changes sequence order/representation and raw context as well as exposure. Following switch validation loss drops below baseline: visually ~0.78 vs ~0.80 immediately before late decay near 90k, and ~0.74 vs ~0.76 at 100k. These are approximate from curves, not proof of independent throughput causation.
- **/0118 / boundaries:** binary embeddings for BPE starts or ends are added to byte input; §5.3 claims start boundaries are causal and ends leak future information. An offline tokenizer can revise earlier starts when a future byte changes previous segmentation; the paper does not establish prefix consistency of starts, hence do not endorse a general causality claim. Fig. 3a end labels have bigger advantage while supplied at evaluation, but are privileged; Fig. 3b training-only 50k then withdrawal shows start-arm post-switch below baseline and end-arm near baseline. Validation during initial intervention is without the hints for the training-only curves; the discontinuities should not be read as identical evaluation regimes. Labels come from an external tokenizer, not a learned verifier.
- ** / position:** repeat subword index over constituent bytes as RoPE position (§5.4). Fig. 4a shows a modest gain with hints; Fig. 4b after reverting at 50k is worse than baseline for much of the remaining run, so no durable advantage established. Since offline IDs derive from segmentation starts, prefix consistency is likewise unverified. Repeated indices encode an external boundary prior rather than byte distances.
- ** / normalization:** keep byte chain but normalize accumulated next-byte log-loss by subword count instead of byte count (§5.5). Figure 5 near-overlap: small improvement, not evidence that changing output-unit family has no effect. Paper's algebra is for decomposing probability under the byte model and same context, not a proof that a separately trained subword softmax has that probability or that normalization turns canonical token path probability into marginal text probability. Variable M/N across batches can alter weighting, not just a global learning-rate factor.
- ** / subword prediction:** temporary separate next-subword softmax targets at end-of-subword states for 50k then revert to byte output (§5.6); Figure 6 remains worse near 100k (~.79 vs ~.76), with transition/unused-head confounds. It is not a negative result on all multi-byte prediction or a proven exact byte likelihood. BPE-derived target boundaries and training-time head create a different supervision budget.


**Remaining-field rule:** facts expressly absent in the read fixed paper/card are **unreported**, not a request to reread the paper. Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. Only reported conditions support this record.

**[R04/BIW-0080](../03_reading/R04/BIW-0080.md):** **, :** §4.1 evaluates 128 tokenizations/document on multi-host TPU, 15–30 min/dataset; 500 documents per English/German WMT/Wiki set, 500 English CustomNews/arXiv and 200 German mC4. Table 1: English arXiv canonical 179.20 versus 175.87 consistent WOR+1-best and 175.98 n-best; German mC4 194.02 versus 192.84 and 192.21 respectively. Finite-sample estimates can score worse than the single best (e.g. English arXiv consistent WR 176.38 but German mC4 206.89), illustrating variance/support/proposal effects rather than contradiction of a true nonnegative path sum. Training text exposure, model parameter/FLOP totals and TPU count are not reported here.
- **:** §4.2/Figure 2 reports document-level Spearman correlation of tokenization entropy with marginal gap 0.57 English, 0.49 German, but large gaps can occur at low entropy. Table 2: on English arXiv, all-word first/same/different-segmentation subsequent losses 9.94/3.97/14.93. This is a conditional observational analysis, not proof that enforcing consistency improves model training. §4.4/Figure 3 finds roughly five candidates dominate an oracle reordering of 128 n-best candidates, not that five arbitrary samples suffice.
- Normalization, de-duplication across paths and explicit final EOS matter for any claimed text probability. This is completed-document marginalization over alternative paths, not BIW-0088's conditional byte-prefix conversion; their different support assumptions must be stated when comparing them.

<a id="BIP-0274"></a>
## BIP-0274 — Encoding a text prefix as tokens conditions on a narrower event than simply observing those characters

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0132](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0132) — Understanding and Mitigating Tokenization Bias in Language Models. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Encoding a text prefix as tokens conditions on a narrower event than simply observing those characters
- **One-sentence solution:** explicitly distinguish raw-string prefix events from canonical-token prefix events before computing next-character probabilities.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **E:** probability-space event definitions and Markov-chain construction expose the mismatch. **A:** not proof tokenization is information-theoretically lossy.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** Genericcharacterprefix (toyA/B), MPE/BPEtokens / existingcausaltokenLM / underlying-symbolconditional / unchangednext-tokenLM, mask/renormalizationchangesneuralprocess.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R04/BIW-0132](../03_reading/R04/BIW-0132.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R04/BIW-0132](../03_reading/R04/BIW-0132.md):** **:** A string-prefix query and the token-prefix obtained by encoding that string are generally different conditional events; for maximum-prefix encoding (MPE), find a stable boundary and exactly sum compatible token prefixes with branch/pass recursion under the stated canonical-support assumptions (§§2–3).
- **Counterexample (§2.2, Figure 1):** alphabet A/B, vocabulary A/B/AA and deterministic longest-prefix encoding: given the *token* A, an ideal model next predicts B with probability 1 because an AA continuation would have merged, whereas a raw text prefix A can continue with A at positive source probability. This mismatch can persist with perfect training because the queried events differ; it does not mean training cannot improve any learned representation or any other tokenization bias. Noncanonical token sequences are “invalid” under that encoder, not invalid Unicode or UTF-8.
- A stable `V*` token is not a substring of any other vocabulary token. Under the paper's MPE assumptions, conditioning on its encoded token prefix equals conditioning on the corresponding character prefix. Divide two probabilities of extensions after the most recent stable boundary (§3.1), assuming nonzero denominator and a suitable initial boundary. MPC (§3.2, Algorithm 1, Appendix E) branches by summing next tokens beginning with the remaining query, and passes by recursively scoring the unique MPE-selected shorter token. Complexity is linear in query length measured in model calls, not constant in vocabulary scans, prompt length, walltime, or KV-memory.
- **:** BPE can revise a preceding prefix segmentation (Appendix H cites `hello` vs `hellow`), so greedy MPE recursion cannot simply be transferred. H.1–H.3 instead enumerate valid covering encodings backward, multiply canonical-prefix probability by last-token probability, sum disjoint covers, and obtain conditional ratios. Maximum token length can bound candidate starting positions, but the paper's Algorithm 2 describes iterating over positions and does not establish a constant total runtime. Its algorithm and prose differ on explicitly checking candidate validity: correctness requires applying the described validity condition/zeroing invalid mass.
- **Real neural model caveat (§2, Appendix G):** The ideal induced token process has zero probability on invalid continuations and undefined conditional distributions after invalid prefixes. A softmax model usually assigns positive mass; Appendix G proposes masking these events and renormalizing, with KL/canonical-token likelihood non-worsening under ground-truth-zero assumptions. That is a changed model, not exact marginalization of all noncanonical paths of the original unmodified neural model. The stable-boundary/refactoring claim must not be generalized from the deterministic canonical process to an arbitrary unmasked neural process. No lossless claim for normalization, UNK or undocumented pretokenizers.


**Remaining-field rule:** facts expressly absent in the read fixed paper/card are **unreported**, not a request to reread the paper. Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. Only reported conditions support this record.

- **Source mapping (preserved):** [S08-R033](../01_discovery/S08/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 57).
- **Manual multi-label assignment:** [C11](TAXONOMY.md#C11).

<a id="BIP-0276"></a>
## BIP-0276 — In-vocabulary strings are generally more frequent, so naive probability differences do not estimate token inclusion's effect

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0133](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0133) — Causal Estimation of Tokenisation Bias. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** In-vocabulary strings are generally more frequent, so naive probability differences do not estimate token inclusion's effect
- **One-sentence solution:** compare strings near an exogenous vocabulary-rank cutoff using regression discontinuity.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **E:** potential outcomes, quasi-experimental regression-discontinuity design, local regression. Statistical technique, not neural causal attention. **A:** no randomized vocabulary trial claimed.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** Surface spans/byte-derivedBPEpretokenization / causalsubword LM / contextualspanlogscoreinnats / nexttokenCE plusstatisticalRDvocabulary-membershipeffectestimation, not byteARexperiment.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R04/BIW-0133](../03_reading/R04/BIW-0133.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R04/BIW-0133](../03_reading/R04/BIW-0133.md):** **:** Vocabulary choice and word frequency are entangled, so a naive comparison of in/out-of-vocabulary items confounds treatment; the authors use regression discontinuity near a predetermined vocabulary merge-rank cutoff to estimate a *local* effect of membership on average contextual character-span log probability (§§3–4).
- Treatment W=1 iff a subword is included; the outcome averages log probability of its surface span across observed contexts. Potential outcomes refer to models trained with versus without the vocabulary item. Merge index is **discrete**, not a continuous randomized covariate; identification invokes continuity of both potential-outcome conditional expectations, consistency, exogenous cutoff, an adequately specified local fit, and an approximation that rank is sufficiently fine-grained. Appendix C excludes nested subwords to reduce violation of no-interference; this does not independently establish it. Eq. 7 scores canonical token paths under a no-prefix-mismatch assumption; finite model noncanonical mass and tokenizer normalization are not fully audited here.
- The paper specifies a 5k-subword window around the cutoff and uses linear least squares (Appendix C Eq. 30); the exact number on each side, eligible near-cutoff sample sizes, and numerical confidence interval for 2.88 are not reported. Figure 5/Appendix D Fig. 7 uses shaded **standard errors**, unstable below 500 and apparently stabilizing with ≥1k on each side; Figure 9 shows LOESS curves with confidence bands, not a stated numerical 95% CI for the headline estimate. Rank-dependent confounders, overlapping treatments, finite bandwidth and structural model constraints remain concerns even if cutoff was chosen in advance.
- **Units:** Underlying text is a generic alphabet called characters (may denote bytes, code points or graphemes); actual tokenizer uses byte-level pretokenization and byte alphabet (Appendix C), internal input/labels and autoregressive output are subwords, and reported outcome is contextual log-probability of a surface span in nats. The character sequence formalism explicitly includes EOS for completed strings, whereas the empirical outcome concerns span continuations, not an EOS-normalized document score. Causal **treatment** is a statistical intervention on vocabulary membership; it is unrelated to causally masked attention or the different prefix-event mismatch in BIW-0132/0088.
- **AI components:** Llama-2-style autoregressive Transformer trained on next-token prediction, AdamW, learning rate 6e−4, β=(.9,.95), decay .1, warmup/stable/cosine-decay schedule, 2048-token context, batch 128, 50k steps, same seed, checkpoints every 2k (Appendix C). Default 57M is non-embedding parameter count, 6 layers, 24 attention heads, hidden 768. Input/output embeddings are tied for default 57M; a separate 100M FineWeb-Edu comparison explicitly has tied and untied input/output variants. No claim about attention-head sharing, interlayer tying or separately shared multi-byte heads.


**Remaining-field rule:** facts expressly absent in the read fixed paper/card are **unreported**, not a request to reread the paper. Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. Only reported conditions support this record.

## BIP-0277 — One label conflates prefix-event misuse with learned vocabulary effects

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0133](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0133) — Causal Estimation of Tokenisation Bias. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** One label conflates prefix-event misuse with learned vocabulary effects
- **One-sentence solution:** separate the prefix-mismatch estimand from the vocabulary-inclusion treatment and test cutoff-estimator robustness.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **E:** explicit competing definitions in footnote5; bandwidth and functional-form robustness checks. **A:** terminology reconciliation is our synthesis, not a new empirical result.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** Surface spans/byte-derivedBPEpretokenization / causalsubword LM / contextualspanlogscoreinnats / nexttokenCE plusstatisticalRDvocabulary-membershipeffectestimation, not byteARexperiment.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R04/BIW-0133](../03_reading/R04/BIW-0133.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R04/BIW-0133](../03_reading/R04/BIW-0133.md):** Default 57M BPE, K=32k, MiniPile, 50k steps: Figure 2 estimates +2.88 nats, fitted −7.72 versus −10.60, ≈17.8-fold ratio of exponentiated **mean log scores** near cutoff, not a guaranteed 17× ratio for each item. Median effect 1.52; standard-deviation effect −3.17, interquartile-range −4.42. Local results depend on above assumptions; headline ≈17 is not a universal byte-LM effect (§6).
- Figure 6 visually gives 8k/32k/128k mean effects 1.05/2.88/2.81 nats; Figure 8 gives BPE/BPE2WP/WordPiece 2.88/3.14/2.51. Fig. 4 indicates smaller effects in 340M/850M relative to 57M but not disappearance, with trends across training different from those across tokenizer choices. Figure 4's ties, size and corpus vary together in some curves: do not assert a clean tying-only causal effect from the plot.
- MiniPile is 6 GB, 1M training and 10k validation documents; separate 100M variants train on 20B FineWeb-Edu tokens and evaluate MiniPile. Experiments use an A100 80 GB server; total FLOPs, walltimes and actual eligible observations are unreported. Mostly English and small models. The apparent growing effect during training is not a theorem that more training increases all tokenization biases; perfect distribution matching yields zero effect in Theorem 1, while Theorem 2's approximately uniform initialization produces roughly log vocabulary-size bias (Appendix B).
- **:** compare correctly matched interventions, budgets, and local samples; this paper is a counterexample to claims that vocabulary inclusion is always irrelevant, not a direct test of native-byte architecture or a guarantee of benefits from enlarging vocabularies.

<a id="BIP-0278"></a>
## BIP-0278 — Token distributions from models with different vocabularies cannot be directly averaged

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Interpret controls, diagnostics, negative findings and theory under their actual type, not homogeneous success count.
- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0088](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0088) — Exact Byte-Level Probabilities from Tokenized Language Models for FIM-Tasks and Model Ensembles. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Token distributions from models with different vocabularies cannot be directly averaged
- **One-sentence solution:** convert them to a common byte-probability interface before ensembling.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** **E:** probabilistic interface conversion plus model ensembling; technique operates at probability output, not embedding sharing. **A:** none.
- **Technique attribution:** Author-used mechanism: the technique field names the method actually used/reported at its declared source depth; no genealogical borrowing is inferred unless explicitly cited. Classification, analogy, algebraic applicability and cross-paper relationships are analyst interpretation, not additional author-implemented modules. Non-neural measurement/standards are labeled as such.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision (current):** UTF-8byteprefix/controltokens / existingcausalsubword LM andcoverstates / correctednext-byteconditional / pretrainednext-tokenmodel, nofurthertraining; canonical-support/corrected-processassumptions explicit.
- **Learning / causal permissions — current:** [R04/BIW-0088](../03_reading/R04/BIW-0088.md) supplies the actual objective, visible context, shifts and sampling policy. These are stated with their sections below; no deployment inference from model family.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R04/BIW-0088](../03_reading/R04/BIW-0088.md):** **, :** A prompt may end inside the token that would encode a completed string, making canonical-token-prefix conditioning narrower than raw-byte-prefix conditioning; enumerate mutually exclusive token-prefix covers of the raw-byte prefix and use their summed probability to compute the next-byte conditional without retraining (§§2–4).
- The theoretical alphabet includes EOS as a separate symbol (not part of another token), assumed absorbing on termination; text/bytes map losslessly to unique canonical encodings. A cover is a valid token prefix whose last token covers the end of the query and whose earlier tokens stop before it. The byte-prefix event is the disjoint union of covers; `P(next byte | prefix)=P(prefix+byte)/P(prefix)` when the denominator is positive (§4.1, Lemma 1, A.2). The paper's process assumes EOS almost-sure finite termination; positive EOS probability at every step alone need not establish almost-sure termination. Special FIM tokens can be fixed as conditioning events by restricting covers to those beginning with that token prefix (Corollary 1, A.3), but this does not mean the suffix is independently observable to an ordinary left-to-right model: suffix visibility comes from the model's FIM prompt format.
- **Crucial exactness qualification:** A tokenizer-induced true distribution puts zero mass on noncanonical token encodings. Ordinary softmax models can assign positive mass to them. A.6 proposes zeroing provably invalid next-token choices and renormalizing; that improves canonical-token cross entropy under the stated support assumptions **but changes the original neural token distribution**. Thus the canonical-cover algorithm is exact for the assumed/corrected process, not automatically the raw neural model's detokenized distribution with noncanonical paths. §4.2 calls validity checks optional in the incremental step; disabling them is not a universal exactness guarantee. Invalid tokenization means a noncanonical segmentation, **not invalid UTF-8**. Lossy normalization, UNK, independent special tokens and actual vocab/decoder behavior require separate verification.
- **Mechanism/cost:** BPE/MPE cover search scans possible last-token start positions backward and tests `encode(decode(path))==path`; §4.1.1 states at most nℓ model runs for length n and longest token ℓ. Incrementally reuse existing covers and group the next byte of already-covered tokens, adding next-token candidates from the canonical prefix; theoretically one new model inference per generated byte after initialization, plus vocabulary aggregation, tokenizer and cover/cache storage (§4.2, Algorithm 3). No general constant end-to-end time/memory claim follows. A.1 relies on a genuinely fixed pretokenization boundary to cancel unknown initial-token probabilities; not all tokenizers or prefixes have one. Appendix B says an average four-byte token may require four byte decisions; §7 warns about substantial memory. No teacher, new model training or shared output head is required. Head/embedding/layer sharing in the pretrained models is not specified.
- **Units/causality:** Experiments use UTF-8 byte outputs plus control tokens; internal networks and original supervision are autoregressive subword token IDs; byte decision conditions on the raw prefix and only appropriately preceding control tokens. PSM puts suffix before a middle control marker; SPM puts suffix before the unfinished prefix, making mid-token continuation salient (§6.1). The method does not create a native byte-trained architecture.

**[R04/BIW-0088](../03_reading/R04/BIW-0088.md):** Figure 6 p.9, CodeLlama-7B HumanEval Random Span: SPM token greedy 45.0 vs byte greedy 63.9; pass@10 token 66.5 vs byte 84.3, **+17.8 percentage points**, where @10 is maximum over the plotted temperature sweep; token healing 62.7/83.8 and token alignment 63.0/82.9. PSM token 64.9/84.0 vs byte 65.7/84.1. Thus the headline 18% is not 18% relative and not improvement over healing. Appendix C Table 3: byte beam width 1/2/4 yields SPM 63.9/65.9/66.8 and PSM 65.7/66.8/67.7, with additional KV-cache cost; greedy byte vs greedy token is a different decision policy even if ideal sequence distributions coincide.
- **:** Table 1 averages byte distributions of top-2 models with different tokenizers: MMLU 65.4 vs best individual 63.4, PIQA 80.7 vs 80.3. Counterexample GSM8K 55.8 vs Yi-1.5-6B byte 61.5; unequal members can hurt. Table 2 HumanEval top-2 ensemble 42.1 vs best single token score 38.4 (**+3.7 percentage points**), but vs best byte score 36.5 it is +5.6 points; MBPP 53.6 ties best single byte Yi-Coder. These are ensembles with two models and two caches, not free single-model gains. Total GPU time, memory and training data exposure are unreported.
- Figure 2's A/AA/B Markov example gives zero canonical-token continuation A after A although raw prefix A can continue with A. Third-order synthetic GPT-2 6-layer test/Figure 3 approximates planted transitions (100 contexts per last-3-byte state, Appendix A.7); not a large-scale proof. Appendix A.5 considers stochastic BPE dropout, while Appendix E demonstrates greedy alignment can create invalid encodings. Token healing only backs up limited context; Appendix D supplies concrete code failures. No independent validation of the authors' proofs or implementations was performed.

Contradictory statements remain **source-conflict**; artifact/runtime or formal-version equivalence not examined is **unverified**. Specific per-work missing fields are in EVIDENCE_STATUS. Only reported conditions support this record.

- **Source mapping (preserved):** [S08-R038](../01_discovery/S08/PROBLEM_SOLUTION_TECHNIQUE_INVENTORY.md) (line 62).
- **Manual multi-label assignment:** [C06](TAXONOMY.md#C06), [C11](TAXONOMY.md#C11).


**Current R1 source/claim adjudication ([FULL_READING_AUDIT_R1](../05_review/FULL_READING_AUDIT_R1.md)):** R1 probability boundary: cover construction is exact for its stated lossless canonical-support process; mask/renormalization changes a generic raw-softmax LM. Almost-sure termination is an additional assumption, not implied solely by positive EOS hazard at every finite prefix; finite-prefix identity and completed-sequence assumptions are separate.

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Architecture-sharing observation or reviewer metric question, not an author-solved new problem.

- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0008](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0008) — MEGABYTE: Predicting Million-byte Sequences with Multiscale Transformers. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** A generic unknown-tying census omits directly specified sharing in byte models.
- **One-sentence solution:** Register MEGABYTE’s reuse of the local byte-embedding matrix for local output logits.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** One local embedding matrix is reused in the byte classifier; hard parameter sharing at the paper-specification level.

### Current card-grounded finding and conditions

**[R03/BIW-0008](../03_reading/R03/BIW-0008.md):** The paper's Eq. 4 and Eq. 6 use **the same local byte embedding matrix for local input lookup and local output projection**. This is an explicit paper-level input/output tying specification, not verified tensor aliasing. **Central correction (P1-04; [correction source](../05_review/DISCOVERY_CORRECTIONS.md)):** MEGABYTE2305.07185v2 §2.2 Eqs4/6 explicitly reuse E_local-embed for local byte input and local output. Global input table and global/local layer sharing are different unspecified axes; paper specification is now confirmed by R03 FULL card, not runtime alias certification.

**Semantic remap:** R03 card’s paragraph labeledBIP-0284 discusses scoring cost, not the stable central sharing record. Current support is its “Interface, task, and causal contract” local-matrix paragraph, Eqs4/6. Scoring cost staysBIP-0169; no ID renumbering.

**Remaining-field rule:** facts expressly absent in the read fixed paper/card are **unreported**, not a request to reread the paper. Only reported conditions support this record.

## BIP-0286 — BPB prose formula requires a targeted PDF/code clarification

- **Record counting/type boundary:** source-specific problem/mechanism/evidence subfinding; not a unique parent-problem or independent experiment. Architecture-sharing observation or reviewer metric question, not an author-solved new problem.
- **Current evidence status:** CORRECTION-PARTIAL wording confirmed; computation OPEN. Source reading is not replication, proof certification or runtime verification.
- **Work / version / baseline units:** [BIW-0051](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0051) — TokSuite: Measuring the Impact of Tokenizer Choice on Language Model Behavior. See the linked work entry’s explicit input/internal/output/supervision tuple and version-scoped source notes.
- **Specific problem:** Vocabulary-size normalization of cross entropy does not by itself yield bits per original byte.
- **One-sentence solution:** Quarantine Figure 6 cross-tokenizer BPB/equal-training conclusions until its original log-to-figure transformation is publicly established; use correctly stated event/byte accounting for future comparisons.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** Probability accounting, not a new AI module: BPB = -sum(log2 p(event))/original_UTF-8_bytes; mean token CE in nats additionally requires token_count/byte_count and division by ln2.

- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** Fourteen tokenizer-specific interfaces including ByT5 byte tokenizer / common causal Llama-3.2-1B-style states / matching tokenizer vocabulary / next-unit CE; choice scoring and exact-byte evaluation are distinct metrics.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** Causal next-unit models with untied embeddings per paper §3.3. Common nonembedding size does not equal total parameters/FLOPs or same text. C.2 BPB formula remains a targeted open audit question.
- **Evidence, comparator, result and budget:** DISCOVERY_CORRECTIONS §5.1–5.3 confirms the erroneous log2(vocabulary-size) wording in both v2 PDF p21 C.2 and HTML. A fixed three-file released-code path at commit 0db0ba5648a4fa4efae010a94f69fc1042a354aa logs natural-log token-average CE; Figure 6 actual run/log/plot conversion remains unverified. Quarantine Figure 6 as cross-tokenizer BPB/equal-training evidence; Appendix F option scoring and G.2 text-budget results remain separate.
- **Limits:** No new FULL reading, theorem audit or runtime verification.
- **Carrying targeted correction:** [DISCOVERY_CORRECTIONS §5](../05_review/DISCOVERY_CORRECTIONS.md), not the old FULL card, supplies this formula inspection. The old TokSuite card did not certify C.2 or Figure 6 computation; no new FULL credited.

**Central correction (P1-03, P1-04, P1-05; [correction source](../05_review/DISCOVERY_CORRECTIONS.md)):** TokSuite2512.20757v2 §3.3: all14 causal Lingua Llama-style arms use untied embeddings, including the ByT5 TOKENIZER arm, not original ByT5. G.2 common-text subset is Llama3.2/Gemma2/Comma/Qwen3 only, excludes bytes and does not control per-language token counts or exact batch order. C.2 PDF p.21 and HTML both say divide CE by log₂(vocabulary size): wording is confirmed wrong for BPB, not merely an HTML artifact. Fixed public commit0db0ba5648a4fa4efae010a94f69fc1042a354aa train.py→LMTransformer.forward→cross_entropy logs natural-log token-average CE; Figure 6 run/log/plot transformation remains unverified. Quarantine Figure 6 as evidence of cross-tokenizer equal BPB/equal training sufficiency. Appendix F ordinary option score is byte-length-normalized log-likelihood; exact-byte extra evaluation is ONLY Gemma2-tokenizer model,40examples/hours with Latin/SentencePiece restrictions, not14-way exact scoring. Other tasks/text-budget results are not automatically invalid.

**BPB definition:** `BPB_event = sum_NLL_nats / (original_UTF8_bytes * ln2) = mean_CE_nats * valid_scored_label_count / (original_UTF8_bytes * ln2)`. Exclude unscoredPAD/prompts, avoid duplicate-window counting, specify EOS/support/normalization, distinguish canonical path from completed-string marginal/raw-prefix conditional. Figure 6 source-code computation is not established; no new FULL/source search automatically closes it.

<a id="BIP-0287"></a>
## BIP-0287 — Allocate recurrent computation within one observed byte

- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support.
- **Record type:** author mechanism; a mechanism/evidence subfinding under an overlapping parent question, not an independent scientificproblemcount.
- **Work / fixed source:** [BIW-0138](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0138); arXiv:1603.08983v6; Alex Graves; 2017; https://arxiv.org/pdf/1603.08983v6
- **Specific problem:** A fixed number of recurrent transformations per fine symbol cannot adapt computational effort to differing input difficulty.
- **One-sentence solution:** Repeat the recurrent transition at a byte until a learned cumulative halting rule ends the internal computation, then advance one byte.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** LSTM state, first-internal-step flag, sigmoid halting weights and weighted intermediate state/output sums; transition/output maps shared across internal steps (§2Eqs3–9). No byte-position shortening or boundary teacher.
- **Technique attribution:** Explicitauthoruse unless otherwise marked; no inferredgenealogy. Algebraiccounterexamples, taxonomyandcross-paperlinks areanalystinterpretation, not authorimplementedmethods.
- **Units — input / internal / output / supervision:** Wikipedia task: raw Unicode/XML bytes / repeated recurrent hidden transitions within each byte / 256-class next-byte softmax / next-byte CE plus ponder penalty. Other synthetic tasks have separate units.
- **Learning / causal permissions:** See the explicitobjective,visibleprefix/fullcontext andprotocol in thetechnique/evidencefields and fixedcard; no bytecausalityinferredfromname.
- **Evidence / comparator / budget / locator:** §3.5Wikipedia explicitlyonebyte→next-byte,256softmax,500consecutivebyte sequences,state reset;1500-cellLSTM. ACT/nonACTerrors broadlysimilar; errors areTRAININGset only.
- **Limits / remaining uncertainty:** No held-outbytegain,semanticboundaryproof or measuredcached/batchedserving established; exactEOS/scalarcompletion unreported.
- **Source mapping (preserved):** `FAD-ACT-01` → `FAD-ACT` → [BIW-0138](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0138); [arxiv_1603.08983v6.md](../03_reading/FIELD_ADDENDUM/arxiv_1603.08983v6.md), method/evidence locators statedabove.
- **Manual multi-label assignment:** [C04](TAXONOMY.md#C04), [C08](TAXONOMY.md#C08), [C12](TAXONOMY.md#C12).

## BIP-0288 — Trade adaptive halting against a computation penalty

- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support.
- **Record type:** optimization/resource control; a mechanism/evidence subfinding under an overlapping parent question, not an independent scientificproblemcount.
- **Work / fixed source:** [BIW-0138](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0138); arXiv:1603.08983v6; Alex Graves; 2017; https://arxiv.org/pdf/1603.08983v6
- **Specific problem:** Halting could consume unbounded work and its step count changes discontinuously.
- **One-sentence solution:** Add ponder cost and a hard maximum to task loss, differentiating while holding the discrete halting step count fixed.
- **Researcher-used techniques and exact roles:** TaskCE+τΣ(N+R),epsilon.01,M100exceptnoted; approximate gradient ignores step-countdiscontinuities, not REINFORCE and not global smoothness theorem (§2.2).

- **Learning / causal permissions:** See the explicitobjective,visibleprefix/fullcontext andprotocol in thetechnique/evidencefields and fixedcard; no bytecausalityinferredfromname.
- **Evidence / comparator / budget / locator:** Synthetic sorting besterror~12%→6%costs~9×computations; Wikipedia10Kiterations,16-threadHogwild,20initializations/penalty,Adam1e−4 (§3).
- **Limits / remaining uncertainty:** Ponder counts are not energy/time; precisehardware/permodelFLOPs/timeunreported. Synthetic task gains not byte-LMheldout gains.
- **Source mapping (preserved):** `FAD-ACT-02` → `FAD-ACT` → [BIW-0138](WORK_CATALOG.md#BIW-0138); [arxiv_1603.08983v6.md](../03_reading/FIELD_ADDENDUM/arxiv_1603.08983v6.md), method/evidence locators statedabove.

- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support.
- **Record type:** author mechanism; a mechanism/evidence subfinding under an overlapping parent question, not an independent scientificproblemcount.

- **Current evidence status:** NEW-FULL scoped support.
- **Record type:** training systems mechanism; a mechanism/evidence subfinding under an overlapping parent question, not an independent scientificproblemcount.
